Proven ability to influence outcomes and drive accountability across teams without direct reporting authority. Experience supporting C-suite, executive-level, or senior business leaders within a complex, fast-paced organization. Demonstrated ability to manage highly complex calendars, competing priorities, time-sensitive meetings, travel, expense reporting, and executive communications. Strong business judgment, discretion, professionalism, and ability to handle confidential information appropriately. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare polished executive materials, presentations, summaries, and correspondence. Expert proficiency with Microsoft Office, Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and related productivity tools. Highly organized, detail-oriented, resourceful, and able to work independently with minimal supervision. job.description: Location: FL-Orlando-South Job Title: Executive Producer - WFTV Orlando Position Overview The Executive Producer at WFTV in Orlando, FL will manage a team of TV producers and writers while working with, anchors, reporters, photographers, editors, and directors to create dynamic newscasts in one of the top newsrooms in the country. The EP crafts the look of the shows, manages story count, flow and placement of every story. They set the coverage expectation and manage repetition. The EP manages breaking news and the speed and style in which we get it on the air whenever news breaks. The person in this job must be a quick-moving innovator who can lead the team in a changing media environment. The EP assists in all aspects of leading and managing a team such as establishing schedules, goal setting, and employee relations and works closely with fellow managers to craft and execute successful strategies and newscasts. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Newscast & Brand Management – 90% Ensure product stays on brand. Manage breaking news. Copy edits stories in newscasts to ensure they are on target with research objectives. Manages story count and placement. Must be intimate with the rundown. Manage story count vs. big story coverage. Set the coverage expectation by holding meetings with producers and conducting newscast critiques. Manage repetition within newscasts and from newscast to newscast. Ensures the product stays on brand. Holds producers accountable on story selection and ensures anchors and meteorologists stay on target with delivery. Manages breaking news. Ensures that we are on the air quickly. Monitors the execution in the control room. Facilitates drills to ensure talent is up to speed. Innovate to match research as viewing behavior changes. Executes live-streaming strategy to encourage viewership on mobile and on other digital platforms. Works closely with talent on social posts to encourage viewership of the newscast. Crafts newscasts look by working with the Creative Services Department. Holds writing seminars and trains new employees. Must fill in line producer as needed Administrative – 10% The EP leads and manages a team of TV and digital producers, writers, anchors, reporters, photographers, editors, and directors. Assists in establishing schedules, goal setting, and employee relations. Physical Demands: A combination of physical work (standing, walking, lifting and carrying items such as laptop computers, pulling file drawers. Document review and computer use, including ability to manipulate fingers to operate computer keyboard and mouse. Expected to work under deadline constraints and meet precise deadlines (including self-imposed deadlines). Routine interruptions and unforeseen assignments are to be expected. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Minimum Qualifications 5 or more years of newsroom experience required Must be a quick leading innovator who can lead a team in a changing media environment Must understand and be able to execute on evolving digital platforms Must be a good teacher and leader Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Must be well read on current affairs and have a wide range of working knowledge and understanding of general interest subjects. Must be able to understand research and execute on the findings. Ability to work well with others and deal with employee issues appropriately. job.title: HR Compliance & Employment Practices Specialist
job.description: Location: GA-Atlanta Job Title: HR Compliance & Employment Practices Specialist Position Overview Cox Media Group (CMG) is seeking a detail-oriented, service-minded HR Compliance & Employment Practices Specialist to join the People Solutions team. Reporting to the SVP of People Solutions, this role partners with HR, Legal, managers, employees, and external vendors to deliver compliant, well-documented, and employee-centered outcomes across Television, Radio, and Corporate functions. This role strengthens CMG’s employment compliance foundation by managing critical programs with accuracy, discretion, and disciplined follow-through. The HR Compliance & Employment Practices Specialist will help ensure workers’ compensation, workplace accommodations, policy governance, immigration administration, FCC/EEO reporting, and annual compliance training are executed consistently, documented appropriately, and aligned with legal, regulatory, and business expectations. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Workers’ Compensation & Return-to-Work: Own workers’ compensation claim administration from intake through resolution, including documentation, tracking, stakeholder communication, and coordination with managers, HR, carriers, administrators, and providers. Advise employees and managers on claim requirements, timelines, documentation, return-to-work expectations, and related employment practices. Policy Governance & Employment Practices: Lead updates to employment policies, procedures, templates, and job aids in partnership with HR leadership and Legal. Drive policy governance by tracking changes, maintaining version control, preparing stakeholder updates, and reinforcing consistent policy application. Immigration Administration: Manage immigration administration by coordinating documentation, tracking cases, partnering with vendors and attorneys, communicating with employees, monitoring renewals, and ensuring compliance follow-up. Workplace Accommodations: Coordinate with ASKHR to support workplace accommodation case management, including intake, documentation, employee and manager communication, and timely follow-through. Gather and review job descriptions, essential job functions, and other role-specific information to support the interactive process. Partner with Prudential to manage required documentation, case updates, and vendor coordination while maintaining appropriate confidentiality. When an accommodation is approved, coordinate with the HRBP and manager to support implementation, communication, and ongoing follow-up as needed. Essential Duties and Responsibilities (continued) Compliance Training & Regulatory Reporting: Execute the annual compliance training cycle, including assignments, launch communications, completion tracking, overdue escalations, reporting, and follow-up. Deliver FCC/EEO reporting support by gathering and validating data, maintaining documentation, coordinating stakeholders, and submitting reports on time. Reporting, Records & Risk Management: Develop metrics and reports to surface trends, risks, gaps, and process improvement opportunities. Flag emerging compliance risks using trackers, metrics, reporting, and program data. Track critical deadlines for FCC/EEO reporting, immigration renewals, workers’ compensation follow-up, and compliance training completion. Maintain accurate records and data integrity while safeguarding sensitive employee information. Escalate complex or high-risk matters and help drive practical, compliance-minded resolution. Year One Critical Success Factors Program Execution & Service Delivery: Delivers accurate, timely, and employee-centered administration of workers’ compensation, workplace accommodations, immigration, policy governance, FCC/EEO reporting, and annual compliance training. Partnership & Compliance Credibility: Builds trusted partnerships with HR, Legal, managers, and external vendors while providing practical guidance and escalating risk appropriately. Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement: Maintains accurate records, strengthens reporting discipline, closes compliance gaps, and improves processes that support accountability and consistency. Career Growth Opportunities: This role provides meaningful exposure to enterprise HR compliance, employment practices, regulatory reporting, and cross-functional problem-solving. The HR Compliance & Employment Practices Specialist will deepen expertise in risk management, policy governance, program administration, data reporting, and stakeholder partnership while gaining visibility across HR, Legal, business leaders, and external partners. Over time, this experience can support growth in broader HR compliance, employee relations, HR operations, or people program leadership roles. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in human resources, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience, preferred. 5+ years of HR, employment practices, compliance, benefits, or related experience, including exposure to workers’ compensation, policy administration, immigration, FCC/EEO reporting, compliance training, or regulatory program support. Experience managing sensitive, deadline-driven processes with HR partners, Legal, business leaders, vendors, carriers, administrators, or immigration counsel. Strong understanding of HR compliance, employment documentation, policy governance, case or program management, and multi-state employment environments. Skilled in using HRIS, learning management systems, case management tools, vendor portals, Excel, and reporting tools to track activity, maintain records, and identify risks or trends. Strong communication, judgment, discretion, organization, and follow-through; able to work independently and escalate risk appropriately. job.description: Technology is at the heart of Disney’s past, present, and future. Disney Entertainment and ESPN Product & Technology is a global organization of engineers, product developers, designers, technologists, data scientists, and more – all working to build and advance the technological backbone for Disney’s media business globally. The team marries technology with creativity to build world-class products, enhance storytelling, and drive velocity, innovation, and scalability for our businesses. We are Storytellers and Innovators. Creators and Builders. Entertainers and Engineers. We work with every part of The Walt Disney Company’s media portfolio to advance the technological foundation and consumer media touch points serving millions of people around the world. Here are a few reasons why we think you’d love working here: Building the future of Disney’s media: Our Technologists are designing and building the products and platforms that will power our media, advertising, and distribution businesses for years to come. ABC News…and many more. These products and brands – and the unmatched stories, storytellers, and events they carry – matter to millions of people globally. Innovation: We develop and implement groundbreaking products and techniques that shape industry norms, and solve complex and distinctive technical problems. Product Management is responsible for driving the overall user experience, feature strategies and concepts, and engagement paradigms for Disney Entertainment & ESPN's global portfolio of consumer-facing streaming and digital products – including Disney+, Hulu, ESPN, ABC, ABC News, Nat Geo, Marvel, and Star Wars. We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager II to lead the evolution of the Media Platform within the ABC News CMS, which powers content creation and publishing to ABC News websites, mobile apps, and digital platforms. In this role, you will own the media platform end-to-end - including asset models, ingestion pipelines, AI integrations and metadata systems - and shape how editors create, manage and publish media within the CMS, ensuring workflows are intuitive, scalable, and tightly integrated across authoring and downstream experiences. This role is ideal for a product leader who thrives in complex, technical environments and brings strong product judgment to ambiguous problems - translating cross-system complexity into clear, scalable solutions and driving alignment across teams to deliver consistent, high-quality outcomes. Responsibilities Strategy & Vision Define and drive a clear product strategy for media capabilities within the ABC News CMS that support digital publishing across web and mobile experiences. Establish success metrics that reflect editorial efficiency, system performance and reliability. Own the long-term strategy for ABC News media platform evolution, including integration of future capabilities such as video authoring, platform consolidation and AI workflow optimizations. Set cross-domain strategy for media capabilities, ensuring alignment across authoring, media, and curation workflows. Media Platform Leadership Define the media object model - structure, metadata, and lifecycle - for video and image assets used in digital publishing. Own the experience of media workflows within the ABC News CMS, including how editors upload, manage, and edit media metadata, ensuring workflows are intuitive, efficient, and aligned to editorial needs. Drive convergence of fragmented workflows into a unified, platform-driven approach. Cross-Functional Collaboration Deliver end-to-end media capabilities in partnership with engineering, design, and editorial teams. Drive integration of media workflows across authoring and curation domains in partnership with product leads. Build alignment across stakeholders, ensuring shared understanding of goals, priorities, and outcomes. Execution & Delivery Translate strategy into actionable roadmaps and deliver in iterative, measurable phases. Lead complex, cross-system initiatives such as media migration and workflow consolidation. Launch products with strong coordination, clear communication, and a focus on impact. Audience-Centered Product Development Reduce friction in editorial workflows, enabling users to spend more time focused on journalism and less on technical processes. Partner closely with design and authoring product leads to improve the CMS experience for publishing and managing media, including metadata editing and asset management workflows. Balance editorial needs with technical feasibility and long-term platform scalability. Stakeholder Leadership Build strong, trusted relationships across product, engineering, editorial, and business teams. Communicate product strategy, progress, and tradeoffs clearly to senior leadership. Act as a platform leader, ensuring the broader ecosystem evolves in a cohesive and scalable way. Qualifications Minimum Qualifications 7+ years of product management experience, ideally in content platforms or media technology. Experience building and scaling platform products, such as content management systems, asset management systems, or enterprise products. Proven ability to define product vision and align cross-functional teams, including engineering, design, and editorial stakeholders. Experience delivering complex products with measurable impact on performance, scalability, or workflow efficiency. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with comfort using both qualitative insights and quantitative data. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate ideas to diverse audiences. Technical fluency and experience working closely with engineering teams in agile environments. Experience navigating ambiguity and making high-impact tradeoffs across multiple product domains. A user-focused mindset with a passion for enabling high-quality content creation and publishing experiences. The Director will determine how Martech platforms fit into the acquisition roadmap for newsletter, app, subscriptions, and paid memberships. Reporting to the Senior Director, Audience Conversion, this role is responsible for driving audience conversion across the customer journey—from converting anonymous site visitors to known users, to increasing paid subscriber acquisition through strategic upsell initiatives. This role owns the onsite conversion strategy, user journey optimization, and performance across subscription products, leveraging marketing technology platforms and data-driven experimentation to maximize revenue and audience growth. Working cross-functionally with Email, Product, App, Data, and Editorial teams, the Director develops and oversees experiences that guide users from onsite engagement, to newsletter acquisition and/or in-app activation and ultimately to paid subscription. This role will oversee the Campaign Manager of Conversion. Remote or Hybrid 3x a week - (New York City) In-office Expectations: This position offers remote work flexibility; however, if you reside within a commutable distance to our main office in New York, the expectation is to work from the office three times per week. About The Team | The Team and/or Brand. This role is part of our centralized Growth and Audience Relationship team, responsible for growing direct relationships between our brands and consumers, operating People Inc. brands' newsletter, notification, lifecycle and onsite marketing programs and delivering best in class experiences to millions of subscribers. About The Positions Contributions Accountabilities, Actions and Expected Measurable Results Own the conversion strategy across the customer journey. Develop and optimize user journeys from onsite experiences through in-app engagement, creating seamless pathways that increase activation and subscription conversion. Responsible for: Converting anonymous site visitors into known users. Newsletter list growth Free-app downloads Upsell from free-app users into paid subscribers. Gating strategy Develop strategy for moving users from free to paid experiences: Define how marketing technology platforms, like Piano and Digioh, support and enable the customer acquisition roadmap across newsletters, app, and paid subscriptions. Develop audience segmentation strategies to determine the right offer for the right user at the right time and how those should be implemented. Own the onsite experimentation roadmap, including A/B testing, gating, and user journeys. Monitor, analyze, and continuously optimize conversion performance across channels Establish KPIs and reporting frameworks to measure funnel performance and subscription growth. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Marketing, Platform Ops, Growth Marketing Operations, Product, or a related field. Experience: 10+ years of experience in marketing, growth strategy, conversion optimization, subscription marketing, or customer acquisition. Proven success developing and optimizing conversion strategies for newsletters, app, and paid subscription businesses. Experience designing customer journey experiences. Strong understanding of onsite marketing strategies and best practices, free-to-paid conversion journeys, ad gating strategies Hands-on experience with marketing technology platforms such as Piano, Digioh, or comparable Martech platforms Proven track record of managing multiple projects at once, driving timelines and deliverables with an agile framework Strong analytical skills with experience using experimentation and performance data to drive optimization. Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate cross-functionally Experience partnering with marketing, product, and engineering teams. Excellent communication, strategic thinking, and stakeholder management skills. Experience managing and mentoring a direct report % Travel Required ( Approximate ): 5% It is the policy of People Inc. to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. job.title: Director, Executive Compensation
job.description: Job Title Director, Executive Compensation Job Description The Director, Executive Compensation serves as the leader and subject matter expert for the company’s equity and executive compensation programs. This hands-on role is responsible for administering and optimizing the equity compensation program at People Incorporated and ensuring a seamless experience for all participants. Reporting to the VP of Total Rewards, this role interacts with Finance, Legal, and HR. The ideal candidate will balance technical excellence in equity governance with the executive presence required to design, communicate, and execute competitive reward strategies across the company. The position is based in the New York City corporate headquarters and is hybrid in-office with the ability to work remotely up to 2 days per week. Equity Program Administration Manage and process the full lifecycle of global equity awards: grant setup, vesting, releases, cancellations, terminations/retirement, and quarterly dividends across multiple jurisdictions and equity structures. Manage and optimize the employee equity database. Maintain flawless data integrity, update employee records, and generate routine and ad-hoc reports. Act as a trusted, accessible stock plan expert to all levels of the organization, including executives and board members, providing support and addressing inquiries with clarity, accuracy, and timeliness. Coordinate with Payroll and Finance regarding equity vests and reporting. Provide guidance to HRBPs and Subsidiary companies as needed. Review, interpret, and optimize stock plan data. Track and report on critical equity metrics including share utilization, burn rate, overhang, and dilution to inform long-term budgeting and forecasting. Prepare projections and provide recommendations on budgets. Exercise sound judgment to resolve complex stock plan participant matters and address evolving stock plan provisions, balancing business needs and employee experience considerations. Proactively educate employees on their equity plans and grants. Prepare and review stock plan participant communications, statements, and educational materials, ensuring clarity and comprehension across diverse participant groups. Own the strategic relationship and service level agreements (SLAs) with external stock plan administrators (e.g., Morgan Stanley), ensuring seamless platform optimization and flawless database data integrity. Act as the technical advisor on the equity and compensation implications of corporate restructurings, subsidiary management, and Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A). Oversee equity plan compliance, monitoring insider trading policies, managing pre-clearance lists, and enforcing corporate blackout periods in partnership with Legal. Executive Compensation, Proxy & Governance Partner directly with the VP of Total Rewards to strategize, draft, and deliver high-impact, Board-level materials and data visualizations for the quarterly Compensation Committee meetings. Contribute to executive compensation-related regulatory filings and disclosures, including the Compensation Discussion & Analysis (CD&A) and related proxy statement content. Monitor and interpret evolving investor expectations and proxy advisor perspectives, regulatory developments, firm strategy and market practices and translate these into practical implications for Total Rewards program design and disclosure. Lead executive benchmarking, peer group selection, and competitive pay analysis for senior leadership. Ensure regulatory compliance for Section 16 executive and Board members and assist in the preparation of SEC Form filings . General Compensation & Projects Serve as a trusted advisor to senior management by providing strategic guidance and execution support for Total Rewards programs, especially compensation programs impacting senior leadership. Serve as a trusted partner to HR and Finance with Compensation initiatives throughout the year. Support the Compensation team by collaborating on Compensation philosophy and with the year-end compensation cycle. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements: Education: Bachelor’s degree in HR, Finance, or Business. CCP certification is a plus. Experience: 8+ years of progressive experience in compensation in a publicly traded, mid-to-large-sized company with specific experience in hands-on equity administration including stock options, restricted stock, and performance-based stock awards. Specific Knowledge, Skills, Certifications and Abilities: Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and quantitative skills with a focus on detail and data accuracy. Advanced Sheets/Excel Capabilities: Mastery of advanced spreadsheet functions (lookups, index/match, pivot tables, complex data modeling) to manipulate and interpret large datasets. Discretion & Judgment: A proven problem-solving mindset with the ability to think critically, exercise good judgment, and handle highly confidential executive data with total discretion. Agility & Time Management: Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, managing multiple competing priorities and tight deadlines seamlessly. Communication: Exceptional communication skills with the ability to articulate complex equity and compensation topics clearly to both entry-level employees and executives. Autonomy: A proactive, self-starter mentality who takes initiative and works independently while remaining a highly collaborative team player. Continuous Improvement & Innovation: A forward-thinking mindset with a willingness to explore AI tools, automated workflows, and emerging technologies to streamline compensation processes and maximize efficiency. % Travel Required ( Approximate ): 0-5% It is the policy of People Inc. to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. In addition, the Company will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. Accommodation requests can be made by emailing hr@people.inc . job.description: Job Title Executive Assistant, Corporate Governance & Board Operations Job Description About The Position: The Executive Assistant, Corporate Governance & Board Operations provides high-level administrative and governance support to the Deputy General Counsel and legal leadership team, focusing on board management and corporate governance. As the central liaison for the Board of Directors, this role ensures seamless communication and meticulous preparation of materials for executive meetings. The ideal candidate is a proactive, highly organized professional who handles competing demands with exceptional judgment, strict confidentiality, and high integrity. Hybrid 3x a week- NYC In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week. About The Team: The People Inc. legal team operates as a trusted strategic partner across the enterprise, safeguarding the company’s assets, reputation, and compliance standards. We are a collaborative, detail-oriented, and high-performing team that values integrity, proactive problem-solving, and continuous improvement. This role interacts closely with executive leadership, the Board of Directors, and external stakeholders, representing the legal department with professionalism and poise. About The Position’s Contributions: 75% Board of Directors & Corporate Governance Support: Manage logistics for Board and Committee meetings, including scheduling, facilities, and virtual arrangements. Prepare and distribute confidential Board materials, agendas, and presentations per established timelines. Maintain the Board portal to ensure secure and timely document updates. Coordinate the collection of reports and presentations from executive leadership for Board books. Track Board action items, resolutions, and follow-up requests to ensure timely completion. Maintain official corporate records, including minutes, resolutions, and governance documentation. Assist with governance initiatives, such as calendars, director onboarding, and shareholder meetings. Oversee the execution and retention of resolutions, written consents, and executive certifications. 10% Operational Excellence: Identify opportunities to improve administrative and operational processes that increase efficiency within the Legal department. Build collaborative relationships across Legal, Human Resources, Finance, Executive Leadership, and other business functions. Anticipate business needs and proactively recommend solutions that enhance executive effectiveness and department operations. 10% Executive Admin Support to Deputy General Counsel , Head of Corporate Legal Affairs & Litigation : Provide comprehensive executive support to the Deputy General Counsel (calendar, travel, expenses, and communications) Facilitate legal operations (meeting coordination, document management, contract administration, budgeting, and vendor support). 5% Executive and Legal Team Support Back-Up: Serve as back-up coverage during the Executive Legal Assistant's absence to provide comprehensive executive support to the SVP and General Counsel as needed including: calendar, travel, expenses, and communications, meeting coordination, document management, contract administration, budgeting, and vendor support. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements: Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Legal Studies, or a related field preferred; or equivalent combination of education and professional experience. Experience: 5+ years of executive administrative or paralegal experience supporting C-suite executives, preferably within a Legal department. Experience supporting a Chief Legal Officer, General Counsel, Corporate Secretary, or Board of Directors strongly preferred. Experience handling highly confidential legal, employment, corporate governance, or executive information. Experience coordinating Board of Directors meetings and preparing Board materials preferred. Experience working in a publicly traded company or highly regulated environment is a plus. Specific Knowledge, Skills, Certifications and Abilities: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Zoom, and Google Workspace ( Gmail, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Slides. High level of organizational skill with a proven ability to prioritize heavy workloads, manage multiple deadlines, and maintain meticulous attention to detail and accuracy. Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to anticipate executive needs. Ability to build strong relationships across all levels of the organization, including executive leadership and Board members. Ability to work independently while maintaining flexibility in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. % Travel Required ( Approximate ): 0% – 5% (Occasional travel may be required for off-site board meetings). job.title: Executive Director, Account Strategy
job.description: Job Title Executive Director, Account Strategy Job Description About Your Role People Inc. is looking for an Executive Director of Account Strategy to lead our Health vertical . This is a critical leadership role responsible for overseeing a team of Account Strategists supporting our pharmaceutical and healthcare advertising business and driving revenue retention and growth through best-in-class client strategy, campaign management, and operational excellence. With a focus on solutions, critical thinking, and analytical rigor, you are a proven leader who can successfully navigate the complexities of the health and pharmaceutical advertising landscape. You will serve as a senior strategic partner across Sales, Marketing, Ad Operations, Campaign Analytics, Research & Measurement, Product, Data, and other key functions, ensuring our programs are positioned for success from pre-sale strategy through execution, optimization, measurement, and renewal. You understand that strong Account Strategy goes beyond campaign execution. You will help your team identify opportunities to improve performance, deepen client partnerships, grow revenue, and evolve our Health advertising capabilities. You are a growth-oriented, positive self-starter who proactively identifies ways to improve processes, increase efficiency, solve complex business challenges, and continually raise the standard of client service across the Health organization. Hybrid 3x a week- (NYC, NY) In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week. About The Team | The Team and/or Brand. The Health vertical partners with leading healthcare and pharmaceutical clients to develop and execute advertising solutions that reach both consumers (DTC) and healthcare professionals (HCPs). The business operates within a highly dynamic and regulated industry, requiring a strong understanding of evolving health and pharma trends, client priorities, audience behaviors, and regulatory and compliance requirements that impact healthcare advertising. The team must stay closely connected to changes across the marketplace to anticipate client needs, identify emerging opportunities, and ensure our solutions continue to meet the unique needs and standards of healthcare and pharma marketers. About Your Contributions: Weight % Accountabilities, Actions and Expected Measurable Results 70% Business & Client Leadership — Lead the Account Strategy function to drive client success, revenue retention and growth, and operational excellence. Partner with Sales and cross-functional leaders to address business needs, identify growth opportunities, and build scalable processes that improve performance and efficiency. 30% People & Organizational Leadership — Lead, develop and inspire a high-performing Account Strategy organization, creating clear expectations, accountability and opportunities for growth. Coach and develop managers and individual contributors, proactively assess talent and organizational needs, and build structures that support the evolving needs of the business Lead and develop the Health Account Strategy team , fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, strategic thinking, client service, and deep expertise across the pharmaceutical and healthcare business. Serve as a senior strategic partner to Health Sales leadership, helping drive revenue retention, renewals, incremental opportunities, and long-term account growth across key clients and agency partners. Develop deep expertise across the Health portfolio, including DTC and HCP advertising solutions, branded and unbranded programs, custom content, audience targeting, programmatic activation, and measurement offerings . Ensure the team understands the unique requirements and complexities of pharmaceutical advertising and can confidently navigate client, agency, regulatory, operational, and measurement considerations. Identify opportunities to improve workflows, processes, systems, and work products, creating greater efficiency and scalability as the Health business grows. Provide strategic recommendations that help evolve our advertising product suite, measurement capabilities, client deliverables, and overall Health offering. Build strong partnerships across the sales support teams. Lead regular team meetings, training, and development opportunities to ensure the Account Strategy organization maintains strong expertise across Health products, systems, processes, measurement solutions, and industry trends. Own the Performance Center of Excellence including campaign reporting and measurement, ensuring the team can confidently analyze first- and third-party data, identify meaningful trends, develop actionable insights, and translate performance into compelling client stories. Ensure the team consistently connects campaign performance back to client objectives and broader business outcomes, moving beyond reporting metrics to delivering meaningful strategic recommendations. Proactively communicate business, campaign, and client needs to senior management and cross-functional partners, identifying risks early and driving solutions before they impact the client or revenue. Partner with Health leadership to identify broader trends across clients and campaigns and translate those learnings into new products, capabilities, processes, and commercial opportunities. Represent Account Strategy as a senior leader within the Health organization, helping shape how People Inc. continues to evolve and grow its pharmaceutical and healthcare advertising business. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements: Education: Bachelor's Degree preferred and/or equivalent experience. Experience: 8+ years of experience within digital media, advertising, publishing, or an advertising agency; pharmaceutical, healthcare, or health media experience strongly preferred. 4+ years of experience managing and developing high-performing teams, including experience managing managers and/or senior-level individual contributors. Specific Knowledge, Skills, Certifications and Abilities: Demonstrated experience supporting complex, high-value advertising partnerships. Relationships with clients, agencies, sales teams, and internal stakeholders. Strong understanding of the pharmaceutical advertising ecosystem, including DTC and/or HCP media, audience targeting, campaign measurement, data partnerships, and the operational complexities associated with healthcare advertising. Working knowledge of programmatic media buying and execution across display, video, CTV, and other digital channels. Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify larger trends across campaign and business data and translate them into actionable recommendations. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and navigate complex organizations with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities. A solutions-oriented leader who proactively identifies challenges, develops recommendations, and drives issues through resolution. Strong executive communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with senior internal stakeholders, clients, agencies, and external partners. Demonstrated commercial mindset with an understanding of how strong client service, campaign performance, and strategic partnership contribute to retention and revenue growth. Driven to make things happen while consistently acting with integrity, professionalism, and respect for others. % Travel Required ( Approximate ): 20% It is the policy of People Inc. to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. job.title: GSOC Coordinator
job.description: Job Title GSOC Coordinator Job Description About The Position | Major Goals and Objectives and Location Requirements: People Inc. is seeking an experienced GSOC Coordinator to serve as a trusted operational resource within the Global Security Operations Center. This position performs the full range of GSOC operator duties while also supporting advanced enterprise security work involving intelligence, investigations, travel security, executive protection, and crisis management. Reporting to the Manager, GSOC & Intelligence, the Coordinator operates security systems, manages incidents and communications, conducts research and assessments, and supports sensitive security matters requiring sound judgment, discretion, strong writing, and independent decision-making. Schedule Requirements: Full In-Office In-office Expectations: This position is a fully in-office role due to the nature of the work being done. About The Team | The Team and/or Brand: The Security team at People Inc. is responsible for ensuring the safety and security of employees, facilities, and assets across all office site locations. The team partners closely with contracted security staff, reception, facilities, event teams, and law enforcement agencies to deliver a consistent and resilient security program. About The Position’s Contributions: GSOC and Site Security Operations Operate the GSOC and continuously monitor alarms, CCTV, access control, life-safety systems, and other enterprise security technologies. Receive, assess, document, and coordinate the response to security incidents, emergencies, system alerts, and requests for assistance. Dispatch security personnel, maintain communications with field operations, and ensure timely escalation to Security Management and appropriate business partners. Prepare and distribute mass notifications, emergency communications, incident updates, and other enterprise security messages when authorized. Support access-control administration, video review, incident documentation, daily logs, shift turnover, and security-system troubleshooting. Intelligence and Investigative Support Conduct open-source intelligence research, social media monitoring, threat-actor research, and other authorized intelligence collection in support of active security matters. Assist with threat assessments, workplace violence concerns, criminal and administrative investigations, background research, and investigative case support. Support executive and brand threat monitoring by identifying, documenting, and escalating information that may indicate risk to employees, executives, offices, events, or company operations. Produce clear, accurate, and timely incident reports, intelligence summaries, investigative memoranda, and executive-ready briefing materials. Travel, Executive, and Crisis Support Monitor employee and executive travel, assess destination and geopolitical risk, and support traveler accountability during incidents or emergencies. Provide operational and intelligence support for executive travel, protective operations, corporate events, and other elevated-risk activities. Monitor global incidents, severe weather, civil unrest, geopolitical developments, and other events that could affect company personnel or operations. Support crisis activations through situational awareness, communications, incident tracking, escalation, and preparation of situation reports. Program and Operational Support Work closely with Security Operations personnel to coordinate field response, information sharing, and operational support during incidents and special events. Support the Manager, GSOC & Intelligence with program documentation, procedures, audits, metrics, training materials, and special projects. Handle sensitive company, employee, investigative, and executive information with discretion and in accordance with established protocols. Maintain a professional, service-oriented approach when assisting employees, executives, visitors, law enforcement, vendors, and business partners. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements: Education: Bachelor's degree in criminal justice, intelligence studies, security management, emergency management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Required Qualifications Minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in law enforcement, intelligence, investigations, corporate security, military service, emergency management, or a related public safety field. Demonstrated experience with investigations, intelligence research, threat assessments, analytical research, or other complex security work beyond routine monitoring and dispatch. Ability to independently operate a command center environment, manage competing priorities, assess incomplete information, and make timely, defensible decisions. Excellent written communication and report-writing skills, including the ability to organize complex information into concise operational or executive summaries. Strong judgment, discretion, attention to detail, and ability to handle sensitive or confidential information. Working knowledge of CCTV, access control, alarm monitoring, incident management, mass notification, and common GSOC or physical security technologies. Strong computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office and the ability to learn investigative, intelligence, travel-monitoring, and security-system platforms. Ability to successfully complete required pre-employment screening and obtain required certifications after hire. Preferred Qualifications Prior law enforcement experience, particularly in investigations, intelligence, detective operations, emergency response, or command-center functions. Experience in a GSOC, Security Operations Center, Emergency Operations Center, Fusion Center, intelligence unit, investigative unit, or comparable environment. Experience with OSINT, social media research, threat management, travel security, executive protection support, or crisis monitoring. Relevant certifications such as APP, CPP, PSP, PCI, First Aid, CPR, AED, or similar credentials. job.title: Lead Digital Ad Ops Coordinator
job.description: Job Title Lead Digital Ad Ops Coordinator Job Description About The Position | Major Goals and Objectives and Location Requirements: As a Lead Digital Ad Operations Coordinator, you will be part of the Digital Ad Operations group responsible for launching all D/Cipher digital campaigns. This role ensures creative meets site specifications, manages production with vendor partners, generates and traffics ad tags, and resolves campaign execution issues. You will communicate directly with internal sales representatives and clients and proactively make business decisions that impact successful campaign launches. Hybrid 3x a week In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week. About The Team | The Team and/or Brand: D/Cipher is People Inc.’s in-house media platform and activation team, fueled by the rich user engagement data of People Inc., the nation’s largest publisher. D/Cipher helps advertisers make informed media buying decisions on and off People Inc. content. job.description: Job Title Manager, Growth Marketing Platforms Job Description About The Position | Major goals and objectives and location requirements The Platform Operations Manager plays an important role within the Growth team, ensuring excellence across our email and SMS programs. This role acts as the primary operations partner, translating product initiatives into scalable, testable, and reliable email, push notification and SMS workflows. This individual is responsible for maintaining the operational integrity for email and notification campaigns for assigned brands—from setup through deployment. Scope, build, and launch specific acquisition and retention campaigns, including blast and journey-based use cases (e.g., winback, onboarding, high affinity user flows). Own QA workflows, including link validation, image rendering, data mapping, triggering effectiveness, journey flows, preview testing, and multi-device checks. Maintain platform folder structures, naming conventions, asset governance, and permission controls. Manage data hygiene efforts (inactivity criteria, churn processing, inactive segment monitoring). Deliverability & Performance Monitor inbox placement, blocklist status, bounce codes, and sender reputation across brands and IPs. Partner with the deliverability consultant to identify and mitigate risks—spam traps, throttling, complaint spikes, cold IP warming, etc. Oversee CAN-SPAM, CASL, GDPR, and CCPA compliance across templates, data handling, and unsubscribe processes. Manage domain-level configurations (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) in partnership with Tech Ops. job.description: Job Title Senior News Editor, Current Events, PEOPLE Job Description I. Job Summary | Major goals and objectives. job.title: Senior Product Manager, Privacy & Trust
job.description: Job Title Senior Product Manager, Privacy & Trust Job Description About The Position | Major goals and objectives and location requirements We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to take charge of our data privacy and platform strategy. You will be the point person for balancing our business needs, like audience growth and personalization, with the reality of global privacy regulations. This role is a mix of high-level roadmap planning and deep-in-the-weeds technical problem solving, specifically regarding our Data Subject Request (DSR) platform. Hybrid 3x a week- (New York, NY) In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week. About The Team: At People Inc., we treat reader trust as our most valuable asset. This role is not just building a platform; this role is building the infrastructure that allows our readers to trust us with their data. This team solves hard, "real-world" technical problems that have a tangible impact. About The Positions Contributions: Weight % | Accountabilities, Actions and Expected Measurable Results 20% | Own the DSR Platform Our current DSR process needs work. You will lead the roadmap to evolve this from a compliance checkbox into a scalable, automated system that handles access, deletion, and portability requests across all our data silos. 20% | Balance Privacy & Product You’ll define how we manage data and identity. The goal is to stay fully compliant (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA) without sacrificing the user experience or our ability to deliver relevant content. 20% | Build the Foundation Partner with engineering to modernize our data architecture. You need to understand our data lineage, governance, and security well enough to guide architectural decisions across different business units. 20% | Make Privacy User-Friendly Stop treating privacy as a legal chore. You will design transparent, user-centric flows that actually help our readers understand their data, which in turn builds long-term brand trust. 20% | Cross-Functional Strategy You’ll be the bridge between Legal, AdTech, and Engineering. You need to be able to explain the technical risk to legal, and the regulatory requirements to our engineering leads. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements Education: Bachelor’s degree is preferred and/or equivalent experience. Experience: 5+ years in product management owning backend platforms. A candidate who has worked in data-heavy environments or managed compliance-related products or identity systems is required. Specific Knowledge, Skills, Certifications and Abilities: DSR Platform Expertise: Experience developing or expanding DSR systems. You understand the friction involved in verifying identities and synchronizing data across disconnected stacks and have a vision for automation. Technical Authority: Ability to lead technical discussions with engineers. You possess a strong grasp of APIs, data flow, and warehouse environments like BigQuery or Snowflake to guide fundamental architectural choices. Articulate Communication: Skill in distilling complex legal mandates or technical constraints into clear, actionable insights for leadership across Legal, Editorial, and Revenue teams. job.description: Job Title Senior Software Engineer 1 Job Description Picksy is our next-generation product discovery platform connecting shoppers with the things they love across thousands of retail partners. Users save, organize, and share products they're excited about — and our platform turns those signals into a deeply personalized shopping experience. This team owns the foundational product data, services, applications, and integrations that power the Picksy experience. Hybrid 3x per week In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week. You'll work closely with product owners, designers, and fellow engineers to translate requirements into prototypes and world-class features, and you'll be a go-to voice on architecture decisions and best practices across the team. You will: Partner with engineers across data, web, and mobile experiences to build and evolve the foundational services powering Picksy. Design and implement new services, APIs, and operational monitoring functions. Own production services end-to-end — investigating issues, resolving bottlenecks, and proactively identifying opportunities to improve reliability and reduce cost. Lead code reviews and mentor other engineers, setting the bar for code quality and advocating for best practices across the team. Drive the identification and prioritization of technical debt. Provide thorough, readable documentation for the services you own. Partner with engineers across the org to establish and align on shared best practices. Bring strong technical judgment to ambiguous problems, and deliver high-quality, complex services under tight timelines. About The Positions Contributions: Accountabilities, Actions and Expected Measurable Results 50% Feature implementation: Work closely with stakeholders, product owners, and tech leadership to plan and create new services, features, and enhancements. 15% Architecture: Lead technical design of new and expanding systems; drive identification and prioritization of technical debt; proactively identify opportunities to improve reliability and reduce cost. 15% Maintenance: Own production services end-to-end; investigate, troubleshoot, and implement fixes for bugs and operational issues. 10% Review, Mentorship & Testing: Lead code reviews and mentor other engineers, setting the bar for code quality; work closely with quality-assurance engineers to facilitate feature testing and contribute to automated test coverage. 10% Requirements Analysis: Consume non-technical user stories, providing feedback when necessary, translating into technical documentation, and/or using as a basis for implementation. Experience: 5+ years of relevant professional technology experience. Specific Knowledge, Skills, Certifications and Abilities: You have practical knowledge of modern development techniques and trends, and you are eager to continue learning. You have: Demonstrated deep understanding of REST, service architecture, monitoring, and the tenets of horizontal scalability. Experience developing complex and highly available services running in a production environment with SLAs. Extensive knowledge of object-oriented and functional software design patterns, including those commonly used within large web application platforms. Familiarity with HTML/CSS and frontend web frameworks such as Vue or Nuxt (strongly preferred). Knowledge of NoSQL data stores, graph databases, indexing, distributed locking, media transformation, and search engines such as Elasticsearch or Solr. job.description: Job Title Social Operations Manager Job Description About The Position People Inc. is seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and service-minded Social Operations Manager to join the Social Strategy and Operations team. This role will own and improve the operational systems, workflows, tools, access processes, and cross-functional support that enable our social editors to work efficiently across a large portfolio of brands. Reporting to the Sr. Director of Social Strategy, the Social Operations Manager will serve as a central operational partner to brand social teams, Sales, Paid Social, Security, IT, platform partners, vendors, and internal stakeholders. This person will manage day-to-day social operations, troubleshoot platform and tooling issues, oversee account and permissions processes, support employee onboarding and offboarding, and help ensure teams have the systems, documentation, and support needed to execute effectively. This is an operations-focused role. It does not involve content creation, publishing social posts, setting social strategy, or running organic social campaigns. Hybrid 3x a w eek- (New York, NY) In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week About The Positions Contributions: Operational Support & Coordination: Serve as the primary operational liaison between internal stakeholders, social platforms, and vendors. Provide day-to-day technical and operational support across social platforms and tools, including troubleshooting access, reporting, distribution, and account issues. Ongoing monitoring of the team's Slack channel to quickly address and help solve any issues raised by stakeholders in real time. Create, manage, and track support tickets with social platforms and vendors, ensuring timely follow-through and clear stakeholder communication. Proactively communicate platform issues, updates, resolutions, and process changes clearly to impacted teams. Maintain strong working knowledge of social platform and social publishing tool capabilities, limitations, operational requirements, and account structures. Lead coordination of enterprise-wide social operational initiatives spanning multiple brands, social teams, platform partners, and third-party vendors, ensuring complex, cross-functional work is planned, executed, communicated, and completed consistently at scale. Account Management, Access, and Governance: Handle setup, transfer, shutdown, and access management for accounts organization-wide. This involves establishing processes and workflows for integrating social media handles with new platform features, merging social media pages, and fixing content distribution problems. Onboarding and offboarding of new and departing employees. Partner with Security, IT, Legal, and relevant stakeholders to support access governance, account integrity, risk mitigation, and platform compliance. Sales and Paid Social Operational Support Help troubleshoot sponsored campaign setup, access,, tagging, permissions, and platform execution issues. Document operational requirements, dependencies, and timelines for paid and sponsored social workstreams. Social Tool Contracts & Renewals: Spearhead social vendor tool evaluations and contract renewals. Collaborate and coordinate across strategic sourcing, brands, social leadership and finance. Evaluate social tools and vendors against business and editorial needs, and ensure People Inc. is aligned with the best suite of tools to meet our business needs. Manage vendor contracts, seats, and invoices. Social Resources & Documentation: Maintain the People Inc. Social Resource Repository and ensure documentation, process guides, training materials, and operational resources remain accurate and up-to-date. Proactively identify documentation gaps and coordinate with subject matter experts to refresh or create needed materials. Coordinate social platform and social publishing tool trainings, ensuring strong stakeholder participation and adoption. Assemble, present and distribute recurring social operations updates, including platform news, process changes, and relevant operational guidance. Data and Reporting: Work with Business Insights, Data Operations and Marketing teams on social analytics and reporting, including overseeing the build out of key reports in Looker, QA’ing, and communicating to stakeholders as new data and reporting becomes available. Create and maintain key reports, compile data from various sources and/or coordinate data collection across stakeholders. Maintain expertise and understanding of the full suite of social reporting tools, metric definitions and data sources including those from the social platforms and our third party social tools. Workflow Improvement and Cross-Functional Project Management: Identify opportunities to improve workflows, reduce manual effort, and streamline recurring operational processes. Explore and implement automation and AI-enabled process improvements where appropriate. Project manage cross-functional operational initiatives, ensuring workstreams stay aligned, owners are clear, stakeholders are coordinated, and deadlines are met. Translate operational needs into clear project plans, timelines, dependencies, and communication plans. Track progress, surface risks, resolve blockers, and ensure operational priorities are executed efficiently across teams. The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements: Education: Bachelor's degree preferred/required in Marketing, Communications, Operations, Business, and/or equivalent experience . Experience: 3-5 years of experience in social operations, digital media operations, platform operations, project management, media, technology, or a related field. Strong operational judgment and ability to manage complex, cross-functional workflows with many stakeholders. Highly organized, detail-oriented, responsive, and comfortable managing multiple priorities at once. Strong technical problem-solving skills. Experience managing vendor relationships, contracts, renewals, invoices, seats, and stakeholder communications. Strong interpersonal and written communication skills, with a customer-service orientation. Ability to remain calm, clear, and solutions-oriented in time-sensitive or high-pressure situations. Comfort working with data, dashboards, reporting tools, and analytics workflows. Experience coordinating with Security, IT, Legal, Finance, Sales, Paid Social, and external platform partners preferred. Interest in workflow improvement, automation, AI-enabled processes, and scalable operational systems. % Travel Required ( Approximate ): 5% It is the policy of People Inc. to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. Actual pay may vary and may be above or below the range based on various factors including but not limited to work location, experience, and performance. The range listed is just one component of People Inc's total compensation package for employees. Other compensation may include annual bonuses, and short- and long-term incentives. In addition, People Inc. provides to employees (and their eligible family members) a variety of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, prescription drug coverage, unlimited paid time off (PTO), adoption or surrogate assistance, donation matching, tuition reimbursement, basic life insurance, basic accidental death & dismemberment, supplemental life insurance, supplemental accident insurance, commuter benefits, short term and long term disability, health savings and flexible spending accounts, family care benefits, a generous 401K savings plan with a company match program, 10-12 paid holidays annually, and generous paid parental leave (birthing and non-birthing parents), all of which may vary depending on the specific nature of your employment with People Inc. and your work location. job.title: Manager, Operations
job.description: The Operations Manager, Infrastructure Services – Burbank Studio Lot, is responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance, and reliability of infrastructure systems supporting one of The Walt Disney Company’s most complex studio campus environments. This role leads a large multi-trade operation responsible for maintaining critical building systems, utilities, grounds, hardscapes, and trade services that support active studio production, corporate operations, executive offices, and business partners. This position serves as a key operational leader within Corporate Real Estate Operations’ Infrastructure Services team and is responsible for leading union and non-union personnel, executing maintenance and repair programs, managing operating budgets, supporting recurring capital planning, and delivering a high level of client service in a safe, reliable, and cost-effective manner. The Operations Manager partners closely with Engineering Services, Capital Planning, Design & Delivery, Safety, Security, Production Services, Client Services, Labor Relations, Human Resources, FP&A, Finance, Sourcing, and external service providers to ensure infrastructure operations are aligned with business needs, asset lifecycle priorities, financial targets, and long-term campus strategies. What You Will Do Infrastructure Operations & Maintenance Leadership Lead day-to-day infrastructure operations for the Burbank Studio Lot, including maintenance, repair, and operation of building systems, central utility infrastructure, grounds, hardscapes, and campus trade services. Manage multi-trade operations across Electrical, HVAC, Plumbing, Landscaping, Utility Workers, Paint, Mill/Carpentry, and support staff. Maintain operational reliability of critical infrastructure systems, including electrical distribution, emergency power, HVAC, plumbing, building automation/controls, site utilities, stormwater systems, life safety systems, and other campus support infrastructure. Drive preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance programs using CMMS data, asset condition assessments, work order trends, field inspections, and operational metrics. Coordinate emergency response activities related to infrastructure failures, utility outages, weather events, life-safety conditions, production impacts, and other operational disruptions. Conduct routine field assessments and site walks to identify asset deficiencies, deferred maintenance, operational risks, customer service needs, and capital renewal opportunities. Balance daily reactive work, preventive maintenance, production support, client service requests, and project-related work while maintaining service levels and infrastructure reliability. Maintain documentation related to infrastructure assets, drawings, as-builts, single-line diagrams, maintenance records, work order history, and operating procedures. Union Workforce & Labor Leadership Lead a large multi-trade workforce that includes directly represented union employees, foremen, gang bosses, supervisors, support personnel, contractors, and third-party service providers. Provide day-to-day leadership and direction to trade leadership teams across HVAC, Electrical, Plumbing, Utility, Landscaping, Paint, and Mill/Carpentry functions. Partner with Labor Relations, Human Resources, and union leadership to support contract administration, workforce planning, employee relations, grievance resolution, and a productive labor-management environment. Ensure work is assigned and executed in alignment with applicable collective bargaining agreements, company policies, jurisdictional requirements, safety standards, and operational priorities. Manage labor utilization, staffing plans, overtime requirements, contracted services, workload balancing, and resource allocation across multiple trades. Develop foremen, gang bosses, and emerging leaders through coaching, mentoring, performance management, succession planning, and training. Promote a culture of safety, accountability, professionalism, teamwork, customer service, and continuous improvement. Financial & Strategic Management Own development and management of campus operating budgets, ensuring alignment with service levels, labor strategies, maintenance requirements, asset reliability needs, and operational performance targets. Partner closely with FP&A teams to prepare Annual Operating Plan expense budgets, monthly forecasts, quarterly forecasts/reforecasts, variance explanations, and financial updates. Manage labor forecasting, overtime planning, material spending, service contracts, repair costs, and other operating expenditures while identifying opportunities for cost control and service improvement. Partner with the Capital Planning team to develop recurring annual capital plans, incorporating asset condition, lifecycle replacement needs, maintenance trends, operational risks, client impacts, and long-range campus requirements. Support development of 1–5 year capital maintenance plans by identifying infrastructure deficiencies, end-of-life assets, deferred maintenance exposure, reliability risks, and business continuity needs. Use CMMS data, maintenance history, failure trends, field assessments, asset condition information, and operational feedback to prioritize capital investments and justify funding requests. Partner with Engineering Services, Capital Planning, Design & Delivery, FP&A, Finance, and Sourcing to develop scopes of work, cost estimates, project justifications, lifecycle analyses, and investment recommendations. Support capital project intake, prioritization, forecasting, and closeout activities to ensure completed work aligns with operational needs and asset records are updated. Establish and manage operational KPIs focused on reliability, maintenance effectiveness, labor productivity, work order performance, customer service, backlog, asset availability, safety, and cost performance. Partner with Sourcing and Procurement to develop scopes of work, support bid evaluations, manage vendor performance, and negotiate maintenance/service contracts that achieve operational and financial objectives. Capital Projects & Engineering Coordination Partner with Engineering Services and Design & Delivery teams during planning, design, construction, commissioning, turnover, and post-project operational support. Review proposed infrastructure designs for constructability, maintainability, operational requirements, code compliance, safety, access, shutdown requirements, lifecycle cost, and long-term serviceability. Provide operational input into capital projects, tenant improvements, infrastructure upgrades, production support projects, and campus modernization efforts. Coordinate with operating teams to plan outages, temporary services, access requirements, labor support, safety controls, and stakeholder communications. Support commissioning, punch list resolution, asset turnover, documentation updates, and transition of completed projects into maintenance programs. Identify opportunities to improve reliability, resiliency, energy efficiency, maintainability, and operational performance through capital projects and repair programs. Studio Operations & Client Partnership Support active studio production, corporate operations, executive spaces, events, and business partners by ensuring infrastructure services are responsive, reliable, and coordinated. Partner with Production Services, Studio Operations, Security, Client Services, Safety, Engineering, and business stakeholders to coordinate maintenance activities, utility outages, repairs, special events, and operational support. Balance client service needs with infrastructure reliability, safety requirements, trade availability, labor agreements, and financial discipline. Communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders regarding infrastructure work, outages, repair plans, risks, timelines, and business impacts. Provide practical solutions to complex operational issues while minimizing disruption to production operations, employees, guests, executives, and business partners. Maintain high standards of customer service, workplace readiness, safety, and campus appearance. Safety, Compliance & Risk Management Champion a strong safety culture across all trades, vendors, contractors, and operational teams. Ensure compliance with company safety programs, OSHA requirements, applicable building codes, fire/life safety requirements, environmental standards, and other regulatory obligations. Partner with Safety, Security, Fire/Life Safety, Engineering, Risk Management, and AHJs as needed to resolve issues and maintain compliance. Ensure teams follow appropriate job hazard analysis, lockout/tagout, hot work, confined space, fall protection, electrical safety, and other required safety protocols. Identify operational and infrastructure risks and develop mitigation plans to reduce exposure to business interruption, safety incidents, asset failures, and service disruption. Basic Qualifications Technical Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Facilities Management, Construction Management, Business, or a related field; equivalent work experience may be considered where appropriate. 7+ years of experience in facilities operations, infrastructure services, engineering operations, building operations, or a related field. Strong working knowledge of building infrastructure systems, including HVAC, electrical distribution, plumbing, building automation/controls, emergency power, utility infrastructure, central plant systems, grounds/hardscape, and life safety systems. Experience operating facilities within a large campus, studio, entertainment, production, healthcare, manufacturing, higher education, municipal, or similarly complex operating environment. Experience using CMMS/EAM systems to manage work orders, asset data, maintenance programs, labor productivity, backlog, and operational performance. Ability to assess operational risks, asset condition, maintenance trends, and infrastructure reliability issues and develop practical solutions. Working knowledge of applicable codes and standards, including OSHA, NFPA, building codes, environmental compliance requirements, and general workplace safety requirements. Leadership Demonstrated experience leading directly represented union trades in a multi-trade operating environment. Experience managing foremen, gang bosses, supervisors, skilled trades, support staff, contractors, and third-party service providers. Strong understanding of labor relations practices, workforce planning, overtime management, staffing models, and collective bargaining environments. Proven ability to lead teams in a fast-paced operational environment with competing priorities, critical issues, and high client expectations. Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, develop, and hold teams accountable while maintaining a respectful and collaborative work environment. Strong communication skills with the ability to translate technical issues into clear business impacts for non-technical stakeholders. Ability to collaborate with internal business partners, senior leaders, vendors, union leadership, and cross-functional support teams. Financial Experience managing multi-million-dollar operating budgets, labor budgets, maintenance contracts, material expenditures, and service agreements. Experience partnering with FP&A and Finance teams on AOP expense budgets, monthly forecasts, quarterly forecasts, variance analysis, and financial reporting. Experience supporting recurring capital planning, lifecycle replacement programs, infrastructure renewal, and capital investment prioritization. Strong analytical skills related to labor utilization, maintenance performance, work order trends, asset lifecycle planning, cost control, and service-level performance. Experience developing scopes of work, cost estimates, business cases, funding requests, and vendor bid evaluations. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting studio, entertainment, media, production, or active campus environments. Direct experience working with unionized trade teams and collective bargaining agreements. Professional certifications such as CFM, FMP, PMP, LEED AP, RPA/FMA, SMA, or trade-related certifications. Advanced degree in Engineering, Business Administration, Facilities Management, Construction Management, or related discipline. Experience supporting central plant operations, critical infrastructure, utility distribution, emergency response, and business continuity planning. Experience developing recurring capital plans, preventive maintenance strategies, reliability-centered maintenance programs, or enterprise asset management improvements. Experience partnering with Capital Planning, FP&A, Sourcing, Labor Relations, Engineering, Design & Delivery, and Safety teams in a matrixed organization. The hiring range for this position in Burbank, CA is $105,100 to $140,900 per year. The base pay actually offered will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the level and position offered.
