job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

Alamo Records, Santa Anna Label Group, Foundation Media, and OVO Sound operate across a fast-moving, rapidly growing portfolio of labels, joint ventures, distribution partners, and artist deals. We are looking for a strategic, commercially minded Senior Director of Finance & Accounting who understands the broader label business and can support decisions around artists, joint ventures, acquisitions, catalog, cash flow, and profitability with insightful analysis. The ideal candidate will bring deep accounting expertise, strong operational discipline, and exceptional analytical and financial modeling skills.

In the near term, this person, in coordination with SME central teams, will provide hands-on leadership to strengthen accounting practices, including intercompany accounting, financial operations, and metadata management, to ensure accurate and comprehensive reporting. The Senior Director of Finance & Accounting will also be responsible for the monthly close and forecast, as well as the annual budgeting process. As part of a small, flat team supported by the wider Sony Music Finance, Accounting, and IT infrastructure, this person will touch virtually every aspect of label finance and accounting. The role requires someone who navigate a complex organizational structure and bring the technical accounting expertise the group needs. This will require taking ownership of detailed project management and process design and execution. Through this work, the Senior Director of Finance will build the experience and perspective needed to grow into a future CFO-level leader for the organization.

What you'll do:

  • Lead accounting setup, cleanup, and ongoing financial control processes across Alamo, Santa Anna, Foundation, OVO, and related ventures, with particular focus on entity structure, intercompany accounting, eliminations, reconciliations, and balance sheet integrity.
  • Strengthen accounting controls, workflows, and ownership across recurring close, reporting, intercompany, and operational finance processes.
  • Oversee monthly close, management reporting, variance analysis, balance sheet reviews, and corporate deliverables, ensuring results are accurate, timely, and clearly explained to senior management and SME stakeholders.
  • Manage annual budgeting, monthly forecasting, and long-range planning across labels, joint ventures, acquisitions, and new business initiatives, connecting financial plans to operating priorities, deal terms, and profitability targets.
  • Partner with SME central teams, including Accounting, Global Finance, Tax, Royalties, JV Accounting, Metadata, and technology partners, to improve financial operations, data quality, metadata workflows, systems integration, and reporting consistency across a complex organizational structure.
  • Support deal analysis, artist and label investment decisions, catalog and acquisition opportunities, royalty and recoupment analysis, and new venture business plans, ensuring financial assumptions align with contractual terms and operational realities.
  • Act as a senior finance business partner to label leadership and department team members across business units to help drive revenue growth, profitability, cash discipline, and operating efficiency all the business.
  • Serve as a reliable #2 to the CFO, leading detailed project management, integration efforts, process improvement initiatives, and other high-priority finance projects as a hands-on operator and strategic finance leader.

Who you are:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting or Finance required.
  • 10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, ideally within music, media, entertainment, or another complex multi-entity environment.
  • CPA strongly preferred; MBA a plus.
  • Passionate about music, media, and entertainment.
  • Deep technical accounting foundation, including a strong understanding of month-end close processes, balance sheet reconciliations, accruals, eliminations, and intercompany accounting across multiple legal entities.
  • Strong financial planning, forecasting, modeling, and analysis skills, with the ability to translate detailed financial data and analysis into clear recommendations for senior leaders.
  • Sophisticated Excel skills, with the ability to analyze and interpret large data sets.
  • Analytical mindset with a natural desire to ask “why,” coupled with the initiative to reimagine and reinvent processes and improve the accuracy of reporting and analysis.
  • Experience working with corporate accounting, tax, royalties, metadata, systems, and shared service teams to resolve cross-functional issues and improve end-to-end financial operations.
  • Hands-on leader with a roll-up-your-sleeves attitude, high attention to detail, and the ability to manage complex projects at a granular level.

What we give you:

  • You join an inclusive, collaborative and global community where you have the opportunity to channel your passion every day

job.title: Senior Manager, Audience Intelligence
job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

The Senior Manager, Audience Intelligence leads Sony Music Canada’s audience insights function, delivering data-driven intelligence that informs campaign planning, audience growth, fan engagement, and direct-to-consumer strategy across the organization. The position currently manages 1 direct report and reports into a broader regional team spanning the U.S, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.

This role focuses on transforming audience, streaming, social, and commerce data into actionable insights that support artist development, release strategy, CRM initiatives, and fan monetization opportunities.

The Senior Manager plays a critical role in measuring release and campaign performance, uncovering audience trends, to build a more unified view of the fan journey from streaming discovery and social engagement through to owned-channel interaction and commerce conversion.

This is a highly collaborative role for an analytically driven individual who is passionate about music, fan behaviour, and the evolving music data and distribution ecosystem.

What you'll do:

Analytics & Audience Insight Development

• Collaborate with Commercial Partnerships, Marketing, A&R, the Executive team and Audience Intelligence teams with real-time insights to inform artist signings, campaign planning, optimization, and post-campaign analysis.
• Collect, analyze, and interpret audience data across streaming platforms, physical sales, social media, paid media, CRM, and D2C commerce channels.
• Conduct deep-dive analyses into audience behavior, fan demographics, psychographics, and engagement trends to support targeting and segmentation strategies.
• Identify emerging audience opportunities, cultural trends, and high value fan segments that can inform artist marketing and growth strategies.
• Manage product release forecasting and audience trend analysis for domestic and international frontline and catalogue priorities.
• Deliver ad-hoc analysis to support the needs of the business, assist with other projects and process improvement initiatives as required.

D2C, CRM & Fan Lifecycle Intelligence

• Lead audience measurement and performance reporting across Sony Music Canada’s direct-to-consumer ecosystem, CRM programs, and owned fan acquisition initiatives.
• Analyze customer behavior, conversion trends, retention, and purchase activity to inform D2C strategy and optimization.
• Develop frameworks that map audience pathways between streaming engagement, social interaction, CRM acquisition, and commerce conversion.
• Partner with digital and marketing teams, and D2C stakeholders to identify opportunities for fan acquisition, audience re-engagement, lifecycle marketing, and conversion growth.

Reporting, Visualization & Operational Excellence

• Build and evolve scalable dashboards, KPI scorecards, and reporting frameworks tracking campaign performance, audience growth, streaming trends, CRM engagement, and D2C performance.
• Translate complex datasets into clear, actionable business intelligence for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
• Assist with funding requests (e.g., Ontario Music Investment Fund), support new business development, and handle ad hoc data or reporting requests from key departments.

Who you are:

• 5+ years of experience in analytics, digital marketing, audience insights, or performance reporting (music, entertainment, media, or e-commerce preferred).
• Proficiency in analytical languages such as SQL and/or Python is considered a strong asset.
• Experience with analytics and BI tools including Alteryx, Tableau, Power BI and Shopify analytics.
• Experience with music and audience platforms including Luminate, Spotify for Artists, Apple Music For Artists, Amazon Music For Artists, YouTube Analytics and Chartmetric.
• Strong analytical and quantitative skills with experience working across multiple datasets.
• Strong communication skills to build trusted relationships and translate data into actionable business insights.

• Creates an environment where direct reports can perform, grow, and contribute at their highest level
• Navigates a fast-changing industry while helping their team to adapt.

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Sony Music's product design team has traditionally focused on B2B - internal tools and suite applications used by Sony employees, labels, and artists. This role expands that scope. You'll work across both sides: the internal tools that power D2C operations, and consumer-facing artist storefronts built on Shopify, with custom extensions on top. You'll be the long-term design owner of that consumer experience.

What you'll do:

  • Design internal D2C tools including a multi-store management dashboard, batch workflows, and ops data views
  • Connect the ecosystem by integrating Shopify data into our existing suite applications.
  • Own the Shopify storefront by overseeing agency build, then serving as long-term design owner of the consumer experience
  • Build custom Shopify apps that extend platform capabilities (bundles, tracklist display, and more)
  • Create analytics dashboards surfacing the right ecommerce metrics for operators and leadership
  • Lead discovery alongside PM and engineering, researching fan and operator needs and shipping from there

Who you are:

  • You have ecommerce fluency. You understand storefront design, shopping flows, and what drives conversion and trust for fans
  • Experience designing both B2B tools and consumer-facing products; this role requires both

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

As a Specialist, Content and National Promotion, you will have the opportunity to utilize your exceptional communication skills to support the Sony Music Nashville roster of artists by proactively promoting airplay and maximizing exposure and consumption. You will have impact across the business by serving as a conduit for communication and information flow between SMN promotion, A&R, and marketing staffs, contributing to single and album launch marketing plans, managing relationships with national radio partners, and planning and executing promotion events.

What you'll do:

  • Role model SMG’s Global People Promise, Values and Behaviors in all that you do, helping to drive a sustainable high-performance culture within our business
  • Help develop and implement airplay and exposure strategies for SMN artists
  • Serve as a liaison between marketing, promotion, and commercial partnerships in implementation of campaigns to benefit and break artists/projects to enhance awareness and drive consumption
  • Plan and execute various department events including artist showcases, radio meetings and summit experiences, conferences, and award show happenings.
  • Maintain artist and team calendars
  • Provide support for regionals including occasional travel for show coverage, events, onsite promotions, interviews and artist meet-n-greets.
  • Solicit, compile, capture, edit, transcribe, deliver content for national radio & marketing partners:
    • Maintain department content documentation, catalog, and prep site as well as assisting with radio digital music deliveries and various event invitations
    • Schedule and assist with on-site artist content captures, including syndicated and satellite content captures and radio remotes
    • Use skill and knowledge of digital audio editing, video editing/production software, and various broadcasting technologies to record and complete post-production editing
    • Regularly support and execute artist interview, liner, and phoner collaborations with radio partners

Who you are:

  • An industry professional with a working knowledge of the music industry and/or country radio promotion (generally gained through 2+ years of experience working with artists and/or management)
  • A content expert with demonstrated skill to create and produce/edit entertainment content in both audio and video format and a working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and Abobe suite (specifically Premiere + Audition)
  • A results-driven individual with demonstrated organizational skills and focus on attention to detail
  • A problem solver with strong creative and strategic skills and sound editorial judgement
  • A team player willing to work nights, weekends and travel as needed (approximately 1-2 times per month)
  • A collaborator with a proven ability to maintain constructive working relationships with others and ability to adapt behavior to meet expectations and needs of different audiences

What we give you:

  • You join an inclusive, collaborative and global community where you have the opportunity to channel your passion every day
  • A modern office environment designed to foster productivity, creativity, and teamwork empowering you to bring your best
  • An attractive and comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life & disability coverage, and 401K + employer matching
  • Voluntary benefits like company-paid identity theft protection and resources for pets, mental health and meditation resources, industry-leading fertility coverage, fully paid leave for childbirth or bonding, fully paid leave for caregivers, programs for loved ones with developmental disabilities and neurodiversity, subsidized back-up child and elder care, and reimbursement for adoption, surrogacy, tuition, and student loans
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community.
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt, and create what happens next
  • Time off for a winter recess

Sony Music is committed to providing equal employment opportunity for all persons regardless of age, disability, national origin, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, veteran or military status, marital and civil partnership/union status, alienage or citizenship status, creed, genetic information or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

job.title: Sr. Director, Digital Development - Columbia
job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

The Senior Director, Digital Development at Columbia Records builds the viral foundation for projects before they scale. Where the wider Viral Marketing team drives influencer campaigns at volume around established artists and priority singles, this role sits at the front end: developing artists, first singles, early-stage projects, and catalog titles showing early signals of movement.

The work is diagnostic, strategic, and hands-on. Read the audience quickly, map the niches that matter, find and test the content that actually works inside them, and run point on the seeding that puts it in front of the right communities. Once a project has traction and a proven approach, it transitions to a Viral Marketing lead to scale further. The role sits within the Viral Marketing team at Columbia Records and works alongside Marketing, Audience and Social teams from project kickoff.

What you'll do:

  • Own the viral strategy for developing artists and early-stage projects, from pre-release through the first signs of traction, before campaigns move into scaled execution.
  • Build a fast, accurate read on each project’s audience: who they are, where they sit online, what they already engage with, and what the artist’s credible entry point is.
  • Map and pressure-test the niches and creator communities around a project (subcultures, formats, sounds, references) and identify where the artist has real cultural permission to land.
  • Identify and test content angles inside those niches at low cost and high frequency. Prove what works before budget scales.
  • Run point on seeding strategy and execution for early-stage projects: set the seeding plan, choose the communities and accounts, brief the content, and place it. This is hands-on work, not oversight.
  • Build and maintain the seeding infrastructure the front end of a campaign depends on: page networks, community accounts, creator relationships, and the process for moving content through them quickly.
  • Establish the creative foundation each campaign scales from: the hook, the format, the angle, the seeding logic, documented clearly enough for the wider Viral team to run with it.
  • Work closely with the Catalog and Legacy divisions to surface titles showing early signals of growth, and build viral strategies around them fast enough to catch the moment.
  • Monitor catalog and recent releases for emergent movement (UGC velocity, sound usage, search and DSP behavior, playlist and platform signals) and flag opportunities proactively rather than reactively.
  • Partner with Marketing, Audience and Social from kickoff so viral strategy is built into the campaign, not bolted on afterward.
  • Build early relationships with creators and micro-communities relevant to developing projects, where fit matters more than reach.
  • Transition proven projects to the Viral Marketing leads with a clear strategy, evidence of what works, and the seeding and community groundwork in place.
  • Report findings, tests, and results to senior staff, translating early signal into recommendations the wider team can act on.

Who you are:

  • 7+ years professional experience in influencer, social, or digital marketing, with significant time spent on early-stage artists, emerging brands, or projects built without an existing audience.
  • Hands-on seeding experience: has personally built and run seeding operations, not only directed them. Familiar with page networks, community accounts, and the mechanics of placing content at speed.
  • Track record of setting strategy that other teams execute, and of influencing senior stakeholders across departments without direct authority over them.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and build inside niche online communities, not only mainstream creator channels.
  • Strong instinct for internet culture paired with the research discipline to back it up. Fluent across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts, and the adjacent platforms where subcultures form.
  • Experience testing content and reading results quickly. Comfortable being wrong fast and adjusting.
  • Working knowledge of streaming and consumption data, DSP behavior, and third-party trend tools.
  • Genuine knowledge of music history and catalog, and real interest in why older records find new audiences.
  • In-depth knowledge of music culture, trends, and creator communities.
  • Clear written communication. This role produces the strategy that others scale.
  • Self-directed and comfortable with ambiguity, able to move on projects that do not yet have structure around them.
  • Experience mentoring or developing junior team members, with the judgment to build process where it is needed and leave it out where it is not.
  • Experience with AI tools to accelerate research and streamline workflow where appropriate.

What we give you:

  • You join an inclusive, collaborative and global community where you have the opportunity to channel your passion every day
  • A modern office environment designed to foster productivity, creativity, and teamwork empowering you to bring your best
  • An attractive and comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life & disability coverage, and 401K + employer matching
  • Voluntary benefits like company-paid identity theft protection and resources for pets, mental health and meditation resources, industry-leading fertility coverage, fully paid leave for childbirth or bonding, fully paid leave for caregivers, programs for loved ones with developmental disabilities and neurodiversity, subsidized back-up child and elder care, and reimbursement for adoption, surrogacy, tuition, and student loans
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community.
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt, and create what happens next
  • Time off for a winter recess

job.title: Sr. Manager, Business Development & Commercialization
job.description:
Sony Music Korea’s International Repertoire department is building a new commercial engine around global music IP, and this role sits at the center of that transformation.

As Sr. Manager, Business Development & Commercialization, you will turn artist, catalog, and market opportunities into real revenue across physical album, D2C, merchandise, brand partnerships, concerts, and offline activations. Success in this role means building a repeatable pipeline of new business opportunities that expands SMEK’s international repertoire business beyond the traditional release cycle.

What you will do:

  • Build and manage a commercial pipeline across physical albums, D2C, merchandise, brand partnerships, concerts, experiential activations, and other IP-driven opportunities.
  • Source, structure, negotiate, and execute commercial deals with local partners, promoters, brands, retailers, platforms, and venues.
  • Work closely with Frontline, J-pop, and Catalog repertoire owners to convert artist and market opportunities into monetizable business initiatives.
  • Develop repeatable commercial models for new revenue streams, including concert-linked activations, exclusive products, pop-ups, fan events, and D2C opportunities.
  • Own partner ecosystem development, maintaining active relationships with key commercial partners and identifying new partnership opportunities.
  • Build business cases, revenue assumptions, and deal structures that balance commercial upside, execution feasibility, and rights / approval requirements.
  • Track pipeline progress, deal performance, and learnings to improve future commercialization efforts.

Who you are:

Technical Capabilities:


• 7-10+ years of experience in business development, partnerships, entertainment, live business, brand partnerships, commerce, or adjacent consumer / culture-driven industries (up to Senior Manager consideration based on total experience).
• Strong negotiation and deal-structuring skills, with the ability to move opportunities from concept to execution.
• Commercially fluent, with the ability to assess revenue potential, cost structure, partner value, and execution risk.
• Understanding of music, entertainment, fan behavior, live events, D2C, merchandise, brand partnerships, or IP commercialization preferred.
• Strong external partner management skills and ability to build trusted relationships across brands, promoters, retailers, platforms, and agencies.
• Able to collaborate with internal repertoire, legal, finance, operations, and regional / global stakeholders.
• Excellent written and spoken Korean and English.


Behavioural Capabilities:


• Entrepreneurship: Proactively identifies new business opportunities and turns ambiguous ideas into executable commercial plans.
• Ownership: Takes accountability for pipeline progress, deal execution, and revenue impact from start to finish.
• Commercial Judgment: Balances creative ambition with realistic economics, partner value, and operational feasibility.
• Influence: Builds confidence with external partners and internal stakeholders through clear, persuasive communication.
• Resilience: Navigates long deal cycles, uncertainty, partner negotiation, and internal approval processes with persistence.
• Collaboration: Works closely with repertoire owners and cross-functional teams to unlock value from Sony Music IP.
• Agility: Adapts quickly to market feedback and adjusts deal structures or opportunities as needed.

What we give you:

Sony Music is seeking a VP, Fan Engagement to join the global Sony Music D2C organization. Reporting directly to the Head of Sony Music D2C, this role will lead the Fan Engagement function within The Greenhouse, Sony Music’s centralized D2C division.

The purpose of this team is to make D2C marketing a constant, evergreen discipline for labels that today focus their effort on the release cycle. It is a central, cross-label team that acts as an extension of label digital marketing and international market execution — providing D2C expertise, filling execution capacity gaps, and building the frameworks that let others work well — while leaving artist narrative and campaign strategy with the label.

This is deliberately a small centre rather than a large production function. Labels resource their own D2C people for their own repertoire; this team supplies the toolkit, standards and process that unlock the value those teams create. Where a label does not yet have that capability, the team carries more of the work early and steps back as the label staffs up. There is no embedded headcount — the team operates as a shared service across labels and territories.

The VP is accountable for the quality and commercial performance of D2C fan engagement across the roster, and for the relationships that make it work: with label marketing, creative and commerce teams, with the international marketing team, and with partners across The Greenhouse. Much of the work is proposing rather than deciding — the label approves throughout — which makes credibility, judgement and influence without authority central to the role.

The role leads a team of five to six spanning creative direction and design systems, design and production, D2C product management, and CRM and lifecycle marketing. The ideal candidate combines strong D2C product instincts, fan marketing expertise, creative sensibility and operational rigour, with a deep understanding of how fans engage with artists, music, merchandise and culture across global markets.

How This Team Operates

  • A small centre, not a production house. Labels resource their own D2C people; this team supplies the toolkit, standards and process that let them create value.
  • Proposes rather than decides. Recommendations are put to the label for approval. The team holds no authority independent of the label, and labels retain final say on every D2C decision.
  • Reuses and refines rather than originates. Artist narrative and campaign concept sit with the label. The team adapts existing creative for D2C — merchandise creative is the one area where it originates.
  • Depth varies by situation. On a frontline release the team is advisory. Between release cycles, on evergreen catalog, it is the primary owner of D2C activity with label approval. On superstar campaigns it is fully engaged alongside label and international teams.
  • Depth also tapers by label. Heavier engagement early where D2C capability is thin, lighter as the label staffs up — every label lands in the same place.
  • Always-on, not campaign-by-campaign. Label marketing works per release; international marketing works per market, per release. This team spans releases and keeps D2C running between them.

What you'll do:

Creative

  • Build the D2C design system — templates, asset taxonomies and scalable creative frameworks that let labels and territories execute high-quality D2C creative at volume across markets.
  • Establish D2C visual and email standards, including motion templates, content hierarchy, build quality and testing practice, with labels supplying artist voice and brand direction.
  • Produce merchandise and D2C product creative that labels do not produce in-house — pack shots, product mockups, banners and bundle imagery.
  • Produce D2C social assets and CRM builds when label teams lack the capacity, and refine or extend existing creative for D2C where core assets are limited.
  • Create pitch decks and D2C creative concepts that help label teams sell campaign ideas internally and to artist teams.
  • Resolve international asset adaptation, where D2C creative differs meaningfully by territory and is today handled late and inconsistently.
  • Supply campaign creative and merchandising direction to the Store Experience team, who build and run the storefronts.

Product

  • Establish the process linking D2C with marketing, sales and merchandising — the coordination gap labels consistently identify as their biggest constraint, where marketing learns of product and release decisions too late to build a proper campaign.
  • Develop D2C product insight across bundles, exclusives, premium formats and drops, proposed to the label for approval.
  • Own D2C pricing and promotional recommendations across markets, with label approval and international input from the commercial strategy team.
  • Run competitor scanning, launch retrospectives and evergreen product ideation, bringing trend and net-new format thinking to label and commerce teams.
  • Build lifecycle and scarcity frameworks — pre-order windows, limited editions, flash drops, live-show tie-ins, gated access and evergreen replenishment.
  • Ensure D2C approaches are globally consistent where scale matters and locally adapted where fan behaviour, language, pricing, territory, chart rules or fulfilment realities require it.
  • Partner with operations on launch readiness, product setup and localisation, and supply demand signals into the forecasting and insights team.

Marketing, CRM & Campaign Operations

  • Train label teams to think D2C natively — what assets are needed, at what cadence, and which products fit which moments.
  • Build the D2C campaign cadence, framework and schedule that keeps label campaigns on track — a named gap where no one currently owns the rhythm of D2C activity across a release.
  • Own domestic D2C CRM and lifecycle marketing across the full fan journey — email, SMS and owned channels — including automated journeys that keep fans engaged between release moments, not only campaign sends.
  • Develop a fan segmentation framework spanning casual fans, active fans and superfans, enabling more personalised communication and experiences across every channel.
  • Build the first-party data strategy that captures fan preferences and behaviours to create richer fan profiles, and own domestic fan acquisition.
  • Provide D2C budget deployment and retargeting guidance, developed with the label.
  • Create D2C paid media best-practice frameworks across Meta, TikTok and Google, with clear guidance on campaign structure, audience strategy and measurement. D2C performance marketing is a distinct discipline from awareness and engagement advertising and is not resourced consistently across labels today.
  • Define flywheel analytics, channel health standards and reporting — tracking acquisition, engagement, retention and monetisation, and how fans move from streaming, social and owned properties into D2C channels.
  • Establish best practice for loyalty and VIP programmes that reward engagement rather than purchase alone, social commerce integrations, and creator and affiliate partnerships — with labels executing against those standards.
  • Advise label teams on preorder strategy, launch timing, segmentation, local market messaging and campaign optimisation, and drive a test-and-learn culture across creative and messaging.
  • Over time, develop predictive audience modelling to identify high-value fans and churn risk, and prepare the design system and asset taxonomy for AI-assisted asset generation.

Partnership & Interlock

  • Serve as the central D2C fan engagement partner to labels, artist teams and territories — including Columbia, RCA, Epic and the UK — and to Ceremony of Roses, The Orchard and merchandise partners.
  • Define and operate the interlock with the international marketing team, who own market localisation and in-territory execution for US repertoire. This role owns the domestic equivalent and sets the global standard; the handoff between the two requires clear, agreed triggers.
  • Work across The Greenhouse with the Store Experience, Business Operations, Commercial Strategy and Customer Satisfaction functions, whose scope adjoins this team’s at multiple points.
  • Build the relationships and credibility to influence without authority across a highly matrixed global organisation.

Who you are:

  • 10+ years across fan engagement, D2C marketing, CRM, eCommerce, merchandising or digital marketing in a high-volume, multi-stakeholder environment; music or entertainment experience strongly preferred.
  • Deep understanding of music fan behaviour, artist marketing, D2C commerce and fan engagement ecosystems.
  • Track record of enabling distributed teams — building playbooks, standards and frameworks that others execute — rather than only running work centrally. Comfortable moving between doing the work and teaching it.
  • Able to operate through influence rather than authority, and to build the trust that makes label teams want to work with a central function.
  • Strong knowledge of lifecycle marketing, CRM platforms, email and SMS execution, segmentation and first-party data strategy. Familiarity with Shopify ecosystems and D2C storefront operations.
  • Practical experience with D2C performance marketing — paid media planning, audience targeting and return on ad spend — or the judgement to build that capability.
  • Strong creative instincts and experience collaborating across design, marketing, merchandising and product functions, with the credibility to work alongside label creative teams.
  • Experience building scalable campaign workflows, design systems and operational best practice in high-volume environments.
  • Global mindset and sensitivity to local market nuance — fan behaviour, pricing, language, cultural context, release priorities, chart rules and fulfilment realities.
  • Passion for music, fandom, culture and evolving consumer experiences.

What we give you:

  • You join an inclusive, collaborative and global community where you have the opportunity to channel your passion every day
  • A modern office environment designed to foster productivity, creativity, and teamwork empowering you to bring your best
  • An attractive and comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life & disability coverage, and 401K + employer matching
  • Voluntary benefits like company-paid identity theft protection and resources for pets, mental health and meditation resources, industry-leading fertility coverage, fully paid leave for childbirth or bonding, fully paid leave for caregivers, programs for loved ones with developmental disabilities and neurodiversity, subsidized back-up child and elder care, and reimbursement for adoption, surrogacy, tuition, and student loans
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community.
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt, and create what happens next
  • Time off for a winter recess

Sony Music is committed to providing equal employment opportunity for all persons regardless of age, disability, national origin, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, veteran or military status, marital and civil partnership/union status, alienage or citizenship status, creed, genetic information or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

job.title: VP, People eXperience, The Orchard
job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

The VP, People Experience (PX) Business Partner, West Coast owns the strategy, leadership and delivery of the PX agenda for our West Coast business units, approx. 350+ employees across the labels and corporate teams anchored in our Los Angeles office. You are the senior PX voice in the market: trusted partner to the CEO, COO and label/BU Presidents, and the leader who turns their business plans into a coherent, best-in-class employee experiences across the full employee journey.

This is a strategy and a delivery role. You set direction in partnership with the Americas and Global PX leadership, and you lead a team of two to three PX Business Partners to execute it. You join the PX Americas leadership team, and help drive our vision: to be recognized as a people-centric company that transforms the music industry and beyond.

What you'll do:

Strategic Business Partnership

  • Serve as day-to-day PX partner and trusted advisor to the CEO, COO, and Presidents across your businesses, with oversight of the wider employee experience delivered through your team.
  • Set market priorities with each leader, anchored in the business plan and the annual culture survey, and translate them into a clear PX plan across the employee journey.
  • Build durable, strong and candid relationships with local leadership and employees; balancing strategic counsel with hands-on support.
  • Drive operational improvement in how the business runs: systems, processes, new technology and ways of working, workflow integration, workforce planning, and staffing models, in partnership with the wider Americas PX team and Business Leaders.
  • Provide oversight and judgment on employee relations matters with the People Relations team, owning the leadership-facing dimension of sensitive issues.
  • Lead with data, analytics and financials to build the business case for change, including quarterly people-data and insight reviews with each leadership team.
  • Contribute to M&A activity through PX due diligence and cultural and systems integration, with the VP PX M&A Lead, PX Operations, and Total Rewards.
Operational Leadership & Delivery
  • Lead the annual compensation planning and review cycle for each business unit you support, working with COO & finance lead, local PX partners and the compensation team.
  • Partner on the annual Business Planning process with the CEO, COO and Finance Lead, setting the people priorities that enable the strategic plan for the year ahead.
  • Drive weekly people planning and executive updates on headcount, open roles, employee contracts and people shifts.
  • Partner with the PX COEs and local PX partners across the full employee lifecycle, from hiring to exit, including the intern and early career experience for the LA offices.
  • Oversee the onboarding experience of all new hires and ensure PXBPs lead it in partnership with PXOps and the People Leader
  • Own the annual employee engagement survey process, for your business units, from planning and communications through analysis and action planning with senior leaders.

Culture, Change & Continuous Improvement

  • Lead and role-model a strong, label- and business-specific culture through our Global People Promise and Values, one that fuels inclusion, creativity, innovation, and collaboration.
  • Drive organizational change and transformation, guiding leaders and employees through the change curve and building teams that are resilient and steady under pressure.
  • Think like a business leader. Build deep commercial and industry acumen and adapt PX practices to enable our creator-first approach.
  • Advance diversity, accessibility and inclusion at every level with the D&I team and business unit leadership
  • Champion The Learning Collective and continuous growth for leaders, LA-based employees, your team and yourself.
  • Deliver for the LA office. Work with Finance, Operations, Comms, D&I, Philanthropy, Social
    Impact & Environment, Facilities, and Business & Legal Affairs to deliver a strong experience for everyone based there, whether or not they sit in your business units.
  • Raise engagement. Own employee engagement initiatives that lift performance and satisfaction, and act on what the culture survey and listening data tell you.
  • Advance inclusion. In partnership with the D&I team and business-unit leadership, develop and deliver strategies for diversity, accessibility, and inclusion at every level.

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Lead, coach, and develop your team of 2-3 PX Business Partners (PXBP), with potential matrixed
    PXBP reports in other markets. Set clear goals, create access and hold a high bar.
  • Partner and collaborate with local PXBP leads in different markets across the US and globally.
    Ensure cultural connections and trusted partnership, in service of the business and employee experience
  • Partner with the COEs across Talent Acquisition, People Operations, People Relations, Total Rewards, The Learning Collective, Organization Success, D&I, PX Branding & Projects and Communications.
  • Connect the enterprise. Contribute to a highly collaborative US PXBP, Americas, and Global PX team on cross-functional and global projects and initiatives.
  • Ensure compliance with local employment law, data-privacy standards, and relevant policies, with particular attention to California requirements.

Who you are:

Required Experience:

  • 10+ years in HR / People function, including 5+ years as a senior HR business partner to C-suite or
    equivalent executives, leading and developing a team of HR/PX professionals, including a global distributed or matrixed team.
  • You have demonstrated success coaching senior executives as a trusted partner, with the ability to shape, challenge, anticipate needs, speak in business outcomes and influence at the top table.
  • You have a track record driving transformative change across culture, organization and business.
  • You are proven in creative, global, matrixed organizations, moving fluidly between creative communities and corporate cultures.
  • You can pivot between strategic solutions and executional delivery as the environment and priorities shift.
  • You are experienced in handling of complex, high-stakes people matters and difficult messages, handled with integrity, confidentiality and empathy.
  • You are able to hold the whole organization in view while adapting to local needs and nuance.

Preferred

  • Experience in music, entertainment, or another creator- or talent-driven industry.
  • Experience supporting artist-centric or creative teams across different cultures and time zones.
  • Experience leading global distributed teams
  • Bilingual in Spanish
  • Exposure to M&A due diligence and integration.

How You Show Up

  • Self-motivated, curious, and compassionate, with strong business and HR acumen and a genuine interest in the music industry.
  • An influential thought partner who builds trust and confidence at every level and instills solidarity
    across teams.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and influencing skills; drives pragmatic, collaborative decision-making at pace.
  • Effective at flexing your approach in ambiguous, changing environments, moving between corporate process and creative fluidity as the moment requires.
  • A calm and fearless voice in the room in moments of conflict or uncertainty
  • Role modelling and living our values & behaviors

What we give you:

  • You join an inclusive, collaborative and global community where you have the opportunity to channel your passion every day
  • A modern office environment designed to foster productivity, creativity, and teamwork empowering you to bring your best
  • An attractive and comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life & disability coverage, and 401K + employer matching
  • Voluntary benefits like company-paid identity theft protection and resources for pets, mental health and meditation resources, industry-leading fertility coverage, fully paid leave for childbirth or bonding, fully paid leave for caregivers, programs for loved ones with developmental disabilities and neurodiversity, subsidized back-up child and elder care, and reimbursement for adoption, surrogacy, tuition, and student loans
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community.
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt, and create what happens next
  • Time off for a winter recess

job.title: YouTube Channel Strategy Manager - The Orchard
job.description:
We are seeking a motivated, forward thinking, and dynamic YouTube Channel Strategist to join our UK team. Ideally you will have experience advising artist and label clients on Youtube strategy.

This position reports to the Director, Channel Strategy, with project direction from Relationship Manager Lead. The role serves as the dedicated manager for a roster of YouTube channel partners.

The ideal candidate is relationship driven, both creative and analytical, and comfortable working proactively and autonomously.

The Orchard teams meet in the London, Kings Cross office between Monday-Thursday. Fridays are spent working remotely.

What you'll do:

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for artists, labels, and Relationship Managers across an assigned roster of priority channels.
  • Maintain consistent and effective communication with internal teams and external partners.
  • Execute strategic post launch initiatives across marketing, optimization, and growth activities to maximize reach, retention, revenue, and overall client satisfaction within a high touch service model.
  • Provide ongoing, hands on support including programming, optimization, analysis, reporting, content strategy, marketing support, and troubleshooting.
  • Deliver exceptional service for MCN clients and internal teams (Relationship Managers, Rights Management, Operations, and others) to ensure video related issues are resolved quickly and accurately.
  • Conduct detailed channel and video audits with actionable recommendations and implementation plans.
  • Track, analyze, and report on channel and category performance using metrics such as CPM, viewership trends, and audience demographics.
  • Collaborate with Relationship Managers, Marketing, and Audience Development to leverage YouTube for key campaigns and to develop platform specific initiatives for priority artists and labels.
  • Partner closely with the Director of Channel Strategy to communicate partner issues and roadblocks and ensure seamless post launch account management.
  • Maintain accurate and up to date records across internal systems, YouTube CMS, and YouTube.com.
  • Provide best practice guidance and tailored strategic recommendations to assigned clients.
  • Identify opportunities to upsell Channel Strategy services.

Who you are:

  • Minimum 3 years of digital video experience, including at least 3 years managing, programming, and optimizing YouTube channels.
  • Fluency in a second language is highly preferred.
  • Deep understanding of the digital ecosystem and the ability to leverage platforms such as user generated content and social media to achieve goals.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at every level, from C suite executives to interns.
  • Technically savvy, comfortable with data, and proficient in YouTube CMS, Microsoft applications, Google Workspace, and Apple applications.
  • Familiarity with Photoshop, Final Cut Pro, Premiere, Illustrator, and After Effects.
  • Strong passion for and knowledge of music.
  • Ability to work flexibly, including outside of standard office hours when needed.
  • Excellent communicator and relationship builder with a positive and collaborative approach.
  • Creative, proactive, and able to contribute ideas and take initiative.
  • Skilled presenter with strong problem solving abilities.
  • Highly organized and capable of multitasking, prioritizing, and meeting deadlines.
  • Adaptable to evolving workloads and comfortable working collaboratively with multiple stakeholders and clients

What we give you:

  • You join a vibrant global community with the opportunity to channel your passion every day
  • A modern office environment designed for you, empowering you to bring your best
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt and create what happens next
  • We give you the platform to champion positive change, with the opportunity to contribute to our social impact, diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives
  • We provide an excellent range of benefits like private medical cover, a generous pension scheme, life assurance, income protection, plus loads of music industry perks. There’s also time off over winter break

Equal Opportunities

As an active part of a culturally and socially diverse society, Sony Music’s aim is that our workforce is diverse and inclusive. Sony Music is an equal opportunity employer and supports workforce diversity.

We employ, retain, promote and otherwise treat all employees and job applicants according to their merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We apply this policy without regard to any individual’s sex, race, religion, origin, age, sexual orientation, marital status, medical condition or disability.

Privacy Policy

Please click here to read our privacy policy before beginning the application process as you will need to agree to the terms of the policy before submitting your information.

Please note that applicants must be at least 18 years of age.

job.title: Artist & Label Relations Manager
job.description:
SoundCloud empowers artists, tastemakers, and fans to connect and share through music. Founded in 2007, SoundCloud is a creator-first platform helping artists build and grow their careers by providing them with the most advanced tools, services, and resources. With over 4x the music catalog of every other major streaming platform, spanning 40+ million artists across 190+ countries, SoundCloud is where emerging artists find their sound, hidden gems are discovered, and music culture is shaped in real time.
SoundCloud is looking for an Artist & Label Relations Manager to be our ambassador across the European music ecosystem (ex-UK), building relationships with artists, managers, labels, and distributors while helping shape our electronic music strategy from our Berlin office.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Act as the primary ambassador for SoundCloud across the European music ecosystem (ex-UK), building and nurturing relationships with artists, managers, labels, and distributors
  • Educate partners on platform best practices and provide day-to-day technical and operational support
  • Collaborate with artists & labels to create strategic plans for music content releases that increase platform engagement, monthly active usage (MAU) and subscriptions
  • Host artist visits & performances from the Berlin office
  • Play a pivotal role in the development and execution of SoundCloud’s electronic music strategy
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with teams including music marketing, content operations, product, and data science/analytics

Experience and Background:

  • Minimum of 1-2 years of artist/label relations, A&R, or partnership management within a record label, distributor, management company, or DSP
  • Interest across music genres, with a particular expertise in European electronic music
  • Effective communicator and comfortable in front of a camera
  • Able to work under pressure in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment across various time zones
  • Results-driven, proactive, and resourceful team player with a talent for identifying opportunities, developing creative plans, and driving them to completion
  • Fluent in English

About us:

  • We are a multinational company with offices in the US (New York and Los Angeles), Germany (Berlin), and the UK (London)
  • We provide a flexible work culture that offers the opportunity to collaborate and connect in person at our offices as well as accommodating work from home
  • We are deeply committed to ensuring diversity, equity and inclusion at all levels of our organization and fostering a community where everyone’s voice, perspective and experience is respected and heard.
  • We believe a strong team is made by investing in employees through mentorship, workshops and enrichment opportunities

Benefits:

  • Interested in a gym membership, photography course or book? We have a Creativity and Wellness benefit!
  • Employee Equity Plan
  • Generous professional development allowance
  • Flexible vacation and public holiday policy where you can take up to 35 days of PTO annually
  • Various snacks, goodies, and 2 free lunches weekly when at the office

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion at SoundCloud

SoundCloud is for everyone. Diversity and open expression are fundamental to our organization; they help us lead what’s next in music by understanding and empowering our creators and fans, no matter their identity. We acknowledge the challenges in the music industry, and strive to influence an inclusive culture where everyone can contribute respectfully and thrive, especially the historically marginalized communities that many of our creators, fans and SoundClouders identify with. We are dedicated to creating an inclusive environment at SoundCloud for everyone, regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, migration background, national origin, age, disability status, or care-giver status.

At SoundCloud you can find your community or elevate your allyship by joining a Diversity Resource Group. Diversity Resource Groups are employee-organized groups focused on supporting and promoting the interests of a particular underrepresented community in order to build a more inclusive culture at SoundCloud. Anyone can join, whether you share the identity or strive to be an ally.

job.title: Recruiting & Operations Manager
job.description:
SoundCloud empowers artists, tastemakers and fans to connect and share through music. Founded in 2007, SoundCloud is a creator-first platform helping artists build and grow their careers by providing them with the most advanced tools, services, and resources. With over 4x the music catalog of every other major streaming platform, spanning 40+ million artists across 190+ countries, SoundCloud is where emerging artists find their sound, hidden gems are discovered, and music culture is shaped in real time.

We are looking for a Recruiting & Operations Manager to join our Talent Acquisition team. In this hybrid role, you will function as a strategic partner, balancing high-impact full-cycle recruiting with operational excellence. You will partner with hiring managers to find top-tier talent for technical and business roles while simultaneously enhancing our internal processes, leveraging AI to improve efficiency, and ensuring our DEI pillars are woven into every stage of the candidate lifecycle. If you are a proactive problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is passionate about data-driven recruiting, we’d love to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage the end-to-end recruitment process for technical and business roles, from kick-off meetings and sourcing strategies to offer negotiation and onboarding
  • Deliver an exceptional, high-touch candidate experience through clear communication while building strong relationships with hiring managers to ensure seamless stakeholder alignment across the hiring lifecycle
  • Own the operational integrity of the recruiting function by leveraging Greenhouse for interview scheduling, candidate communications, feedback management, scorecard analysis, and reporting
  • Act as a champion for our DEI pillars by ensuring inclusive language in job descriptions, auditing sourcing practices for bias, and contributing to employer branding initiatives

The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience across programmatic integrations, troubleshooting, demand partner management, and yield optimization within web and mobile.

job.description: Department Sales Location Sydney (NS) Stingray is a leading global music, media and technology company, and Canada’s premier radio broadcaster. At Stingray, creativity, collaboration and innovative technology are the pillars of our DNA. As a valued team members prepares for retirement, we are currently looking for a Media Sales Strategist to join our Sydney team and cover the Cape Breton Regional Municipality! This position reports to the Retail Sales Manager for Hot 101.9 and New Country 103.5/Sydney . Stingray offers one of the most robust multimedia platforms for businesses to market and sell their products and services, locally, nationally or globally. Our ideal candidate has a strong multimedia marketing and sales background, and has demonstrated the ability to manage and grow an active client list, while understanding the importance of a team mentality with a desire to be part of the fabric of the community. Located on beautiful Cape Breton Island, Sydney serves as the gateway to the Cabot Trail, the Cape Breton Highlands National Park, and several other cultural attractions. With a diversified economy, it’s the largest urban centre on the island with a population of approximately 100,000 and serves as its healthcare, educational, and transportation hub. Your day-to-day Be a local sales leader of the Hot 101.9 and New Country 103.5, Stingray-owned radio stations. You will have the opportunity to harness the power of these popular stations while also representing all Stingray Radio Stations from Vancouver to St. John’s, unlocking vast sales potential across a nationwide network. Leverage a diverse range of media solutions including radio, programmatic display, programmatic video, connected TV, digital out-of-home, YouTube, search, social, and our proprietary retail media platform – to help clients grow and succeed. Own the full sales process from lead generation and prospecting to client needs analysis, solution presentation, negotiation, and closing. Drive revenue growth and achieve revenue targets through consultative sales and development of strategic proposals. Manage and grow your client base while identifying new business opportunities . Collaborate with internal teams (promotions, programming, creative, production, digital campaign managers) to deliver impactful, multi-platform advertising campaigns. Help handle the administrative responsibilities of the Sydney Sales Department, including building client/station proposals; coordinating the remote booking process/wrap-up reports (for both local and national opportunities); and representing the stations at client and community partner events. Your qualifications You have 2+ years of in-person, consultative sales or account management experience (experience in multi-media advertising or digital media is a plus). Ability to self-manage, proven high-achieving performer in all facets of life with a track record of consistently achieving and exceeding sales targets. You are comfortable building ground-up ideas and presenting your strategies to business owners and operators. You are an excellent communicator, presenter, and negotiator with a history of building strong, lasting, business relationships. You are well-organized, accountable, and skilled at managing time and competing priorities in a fast-paced environment with a team-focused mindset. You live in or would relocate to Sydney, NS; have a valid driver’s license; access to a vehicle; and valid vehicle insurance. job.title: Director of Customer Support
job.description: About Suno We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world. Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible. Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA). About the Role If you’ve spent your career building world-class support organizations and you’re itching to rebuild one from the ground up — AI-first, data-driven, and at real scale — this is the role. As Director of Customer Experience (Support) at Suno, you’ll own our customer support function end-to-end: setting and managing SLAs, running a lean P&L, and ensuring every user who needs help gets a high-quality experience. You’ll lead a team of 6–8 support ICs and partner closely with Trust & Safety, Product, Billing, Legal, and Policy to solve some of our hardest customer-facing problems. You’ll report to the Sr. Director of Customer Experience & Safety. What You’ll Do Define, track, and manage to SLAs across all support channels — using data to surface trends, identify gaps, and drive continuous improvement in resolution time and quality. Own the support P&L, managing costs while scaling capacity intelligently as the product and user base grow. Design the right support experience for each problem type — deciding when a user needs a human, an AI agent, a help article, or a proactive fix upstream in the product. Build and iterate on operational processes that make the team faster, more consistent, and less reliant on manual effort — including launching new support channels. Lead and develop a team of 6–8 support ICs, setting clear expectations, coaching on quality, and building a culture that’s as data-minded as it is customer-obsessed. Partner with Product, T&S, Billing, and Legal to close the loop between support signals and product decisions — helping Suno build toward a future where creative fulfillment is a daily reality for everyone. What You’ll Need Must-Haves 7–9 years of experience in support leadership, with a track record of building and managing high-performing teams. Background in consumer technology — you understand what it means to support a large, diverse user base with high expectations and low tolerance for friction. Experience building or scaling multi-channel support operations (email, chat, in-app, etc.). A genuinely data-driven operating style — you set goals in metrics, track them rigorously, and use data to make decisions, not just report outcomes. Experience managing a support P&L or cost-per-ticket model. Strong process instincts — you document, systematize, and build for repeatability. Experience with AI-native or AI-assisted support tooling (deflection flows, chatbots, copilots for agents, or similar). Nice-to-Haves Hands-on experience building with LLM-powered support tools — prompt design, workflow automation, or agent evaluation. Familiarity with Trust & Safety-adjacent support workflows. Background in the music industry or a music-adjacent platforms, whether working with artists, labels, or music creators, with the ability to speak fluently about music production, audio editing, and/or the creative process Experience scaling a support org through rapid company or product growth. Hands-on work operating tiered support models across distinct customer segments, including free and paid subscribers, enterprise or API clients, and high-profile creators or artists, with a strong sense of when and how to escalate and how to calibrate the experience for each tier Background supporting billing, fraud, or identity-related user issues. Experience running community or self-serve support programs (help centers, forums, FAQs). Work Location Policy This role is expected to work from the designated Suno office 5 days a week, per Suno’s company policy. Full-time employees will receive competitive equity packages, and comprehensive benefits. The actual base salary offered may vary depending on location, skills, qualifications, and experience. Additional Notes Applicants must be eligible to work in the US. Willingness to travel (up to 10%) to collaborate with team members across Suno office locations. Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees Company Equity Package 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k) Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options) 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave Creative Education Stipend Generous Commuter Allowance In-Office Lunch (5 days per week) Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

About the Program Suno's mission is amplifying creativity for people everywhere. Having built strong traction with emerging musicians and producers, our next opportunity is the content creator economy. Suno’s new Emerging Creator Program launches that effort: developing the next generation of creators while establishing Suno as a company that accelerates creative careers. The program is a selective, cohort-based 12-week experience for a cohort of nano and micro creators building careers around content. Members get access to exclusive programming including Suno workshops and keynotes from breakout creators, plus creative contests, content spotlights, IRL events, and a network of fellow creators. At the end of the program, we aim to sign a few participants for ongoing deals with Suno, maintain an active community of creators, and scale the initiative beyond the pilot phase. The Role You'll be the operational engine of the program: building it from the ground up alongside the Suno team through August and September, then running it end-to-end through December. You'll own the calendar, the cohort experience, the speakers, the events, and all of the details in between. In this role you’ll have the opportunity to work closely with Growth and Influencer marketing, Music partnerships and Creative to turn this from strategy and vision into reality. What You'll Do Build Translate the program outline into a week-by-week curriculum: session formats, Suno skills/tools coverage, contest design for off weeks Build and manage the guest speaker pipeline: identify, pitch, confirm, and prep breakout-creator speakers and mentors Stand up program infrastructure: community channel (Slack/Discord), calendar, meeting/tech setup, application intake and tracking Support outreach and sourcing: manage the handpicked invite list, Spark referrals, and application pipeline; run logistics for the selection process (Sept 7–18) Determine application approach, launch messaging, and launch-creator partnership Source and negotiate member perks with partner tools and brands Coordinate internal reviews (including legal review of contest mechanics, creator payments, event liability, and minors) Run Own the biweekly programming cadence end-to-end: scheduling, speaker coordination, session production, follow-ups Run monthly creative contests: briefs, submission tracking, judging logistics, prize fulfillment Design and manage the creator spotlight approach Produce IRL moments if applicable Be the day-to-day face of the program for members: onboarding, questions, nudges, community management, keeping energy high Track program health: attendance, participation, contest engagement, member sentiment; flag at-risk members early Assess Produce the graduation moment: credentialing, culmination for participants Transition the cohort into the alumni network Deliver a program retro: what worked, what didn't, and a recommended blueprint for cohort 2 Who You Are You've operated programs like this before: 3+ years running cohort-based programs, creator/community programs, accelerators, fellowships, or high-touch event series, ideally you’ve built one from scratch. You know the creator economy: You understand how nano/micro creators think about growth, money, brands, and community and you can talk to them credibly. Bonus: you've worked with creator programs, MCNs, talent management, or platform partnerships You're an ops machine: Calendars, run-of-shows, trackers, follow-ups. You're the person who notices the Zoom link is wrong before anyone joins You’re hospitality-minded and a strong experience designer: Members should feel the program is run by someone who gets them. job.title: Trending News Producer - Business and Sports
job.description: Position Summary The Tampa Bay Times is hiring a Trending News Producer focused on business and sports who will join a new high-metabolism digital-first Bay Now team working to produce multiple breakouts, explainers, aggregations each day that boil down interesting news developments. Trending News Producers work quickly and nimbly to make sense of bigger stories or hone in on high-interest topics and trends that speak to our readers. They will put in context various rankings and lists – and Tampa Bay and Florida’s place in it. The work should be fast, sharp and fun when appropriate. A fair number of posts will be aggregations and listicles, providing nuggets of news and information. Though their focus will be on business and sports topics, they may occasionally write trending posts on other subjects. This role will also entail some podcast production. Filming, video editing, and audio recording/editing skills are required for this role accordingly in addition to sharp news judgment and demonstrated ability to write with speed and attention to detail. This role will report in to the Assistant Managing Editor, Digital Engagement and be located in our St. Petersburg, FL office. Key Responsibilities Write two articles a day five days a week on primarily sports or business topics, but other topics as required. Be constantly searching for news to cover and find engaging, locally-centered ways angles on stories. Get on publicists’ email blast lists to find news to aggregate. Receive assignments from across the newsroom. Track the traffic on your stories to assess performance and then brainstorm follow-ups. Produce, record, film, and edit podcasts of at least 15 minutes in length or more up to several times per week. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in journalism, communications, English, or related field. Relevant experience writing for a journalistic outlet, including a student newspaper. A combination of speed and attention to detail. A constant hunger to find new stories and generate traffic. A demonstrated track record of producing, recording, filming, and editing podcasts of at least 15 minutes. Why Work at the Tampa Bay Times Be part of an organization committed to public service and journalistic excellence Support a diverse workforce that includes newsroom, production, and corporate teams Work in a collaborative, mission-driven environment Health coverage for you and your family through medical, dental, and vision plans. 100% employer-paid short-term and long-term disability. 100% employer-paid basic life insurance. Supplemental life insurance. Tax advantages through flexible spending accounts that allow you to pay for specific health care and dependent care expenses with pre-tax dollars. Tax-deferred savings plan for retirement. A generous PTO program and much more. Equal Opportunity Employer The Tampa Bay Times is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the workplace. We encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply.

job.description: Abogado/a Corporativo/a & Procurement Ubicación: Ciudad de México Sobre el rol y el equipo En TelevisaUnivision buscamos incorporar a nuestro equipo jurídico a un/a Abogado/a Corporativo/a & Procurement , quien tendrá la oportunidad de colaborar con diferentes áreas del negocio y participar en asuntos relacionados con Derecho Corporativo, Gobierno Corporativo, contratos y procesos de Procurement . Formarás parte de un equipo jurídico multidisciplinario, brindando asesoría a clientes internos y colaborando con equipos nacionales e internacionales, así como con asesores externos. Elaborar y revisar contratos civiles y mercantiles con diferentes áreas de negocio y proveedores. Participar en la revisión y negociación de contratos relacionados con procesos de Procurement y adquisición de bienes y servicios . Experiencia en elaboración y revisión de contratos civiles y mercantiles . Conocimiento de Gobierno Corporativo, asambleas, consejos de administración, poderes y mantenimiento societario. Experiencia en trámites notariales, protocolizaciones, legalizaciones y apostillas. Conocimiento de obligaciones legales y regulatorias aplicables a empresas en México. Experiencia trabajando con clientes internos y diferentes áreas del negocio. Capacidad de análisis jurídico y resolución de problemas. Excelentes habilidades de comunicación oral y escrita. Capacidad de negociación y manejo de stakeholders. Organización, atención al detalle y capacidad para administrar múltiples asuntos simultáneamente. Orientación al cliente interno y enfoque práctico para la solución de problemas. Inglés avanzado . Experiencia en proyectos de transformación, digitalización o mejora de procesos legales. Manejo de herramientas de gestión documental o plataformas legales. Lo que encontrarás con nosotros La oportunidad de formar parte de una empresa global de medios y entretenimiento . Exposición a diferentes áreas del negocio y diversos retos jurídicos. Participación en proyectos multidisciplinarios y de alcance internacional. Colaboración con equipos nacionales e internacionales. Un entorno dinámico donde podrás desarrollar y fortalecer tu experiencia jurídica. La oportunidad de aportar soluciones legales con impacto directo en el negocio. We seek an enthusiastic and aggressive self-starter to assist Account Executives in their transactional efforts.
