We offer a wide selection of perks and benefits including PTO; tuition reimbursement; wellness and employee support programs; 401K; and life and other insurance plans. This is all in addition to our comprehensive and competitive health benefits package featuring medical, dental and vision coverage options. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location. Please note the national salary range listed in the job posting reflects the new hire salary range across levels and U.S. locations that would be applicable to the position. Tu rol será clave para asegurar la correcta implementación, monitoreo continuo y optimización de las estrategias digitales de los clientes, analizando métricas de rendimiento para generar reportes con insights clave que respalden la retención y el crecimiento de las cuentas Tu día a día: • Coordinación y entrega de reportes post-venta e implementación de campañas digitales en conjunto con el Gerente de Ventas y el cliente/agencia. • Gestión operativa y comunicación fluida con el equipo de Ad Operations (AdOps) para la correcta ejecución de materiales, tagging y arranque puntual de campañas. • Monitoreo diario del performance de las campañas (impresiones, clics, CTR, VTR, pacing de entrega) para asegurar el cumplimiento total del inventario y KPIs contratados. • Identificación proactiva de desviaciones en el pacing o rendimiento, emitiendo recomendaciones y sugerencias tácticas para la optimización de las campañas. • Elaboración de reportes intermedios ( mid-campaign ) y finales ( wrap-up reports ) con métricas claras e insights estratégicos sobre el comportamiento de la audiencia y efectividad del pautado. • Asesoría técnica al cliente sobre especificadores de materiales, formatos publicitarios y mejores prácticas en entornos digitales/streaming. • Apoyo en el control administrativo de la cuenta (revisión de entregables/testigos y alineación con facturación en caso de ajustes de inventario). Tu deberás tener: • Licenciatura en Mercadotecnia, Mercadotecnia Digital, Comunicación, Administración o carrera afín. • Experiencia previa (2+ años) en posiciones de Account Management, Ad Operations, Planeación Digital o Post-Venta en medios digitales, agencias o plataformas de ad-tech. • Conocimiento profundo de métricas de publicidad digital (CPM, CTR, VTR, Viewability, Pacing, etc.) y plataformas ad-server / analítica (ej. Google Ad Manager, Google Analytics, Sizmek, Moat, etc.). • Dominio de herramientas de presentación y reporte (PowerPoint, Excel avanzado, Google Looker Studio o similares). • Inglés (nivel intermedio / avanzado). job.title: Coordinador Jurídico
job.description: Coordinador Juridico Ubicación: Ciudad de México – Santa Fe Modalidad: 100% presencial Sobre el rol y el equipo En TelevisaUnivision estamos buscando un Senior Manager Jurídico – Corporativo y de Funciones Empresariales para integrarse a nuestra Dirección Jurídica Corporativo y de Funciones Empresariales. Esta posición tendrá un rol estratégico en la administración y supervisión de los asuntos societarios de las subsidiarias mexicanas y extranjeras del grupo, asegurando el cumplimiento de las obligaciones legales aplicables y la actualización permanente de los registros societarios. Asimismo, será responsable de brindar asesoría legal estratégica en materia corporativa, societaria, bancaria, contractual, fusiones y adquisiciones y otros asuntos que impacten directamente en la operación y desarrollo del negocio. La persona que ocupe esta posición tendrá la oportunidad de liderar y desarrollar a abogados corporativos y/o paralegales, asegurando la correcta ejecución de las actividades del área y acompañando a diferentes líderes y áreas estratégicas de la organización. Sobre la posición Como Senior Manager Jurídico – Corporativo y de Funciones Empresariales , tendrás un rol clave dentro de la Dirección Jurídica, participando en operaciones y proyectos estratégicos para el grupo. Trabajarás de manera cercana con áreas como Tesorería, Finanzas, Contraloría, Sourcing & Procurement, IT, Real Estate, Fiscal, Negocio y Ventas, proporcionando asesoría legal estratégica y acompañando operaciones corporativas nacionales e internacionales. Serás responsable de supervisar y fortalecer las prácticas de gobierno corporativo y administración societaria, así como de liderar y estructurar proyectos de fusiones y adquisiciones, reestructuras corporativas, financiamientos y otros asuntos corporativos complejos. Esta posición requiere una sólida visión estratégica y de negocio, así como la capacidad para gestionar múltiples proyectos y prioridades, interactuar con niveles ejecutivos y participar en la toma de decisiones de alto impacto para la organización. Tu día a día Gobierno corporativo y administración societaria Coordinarás la implementación y actualización de políticas y mejores prácticas de gobierno corporativo. Definirás los criterios que rigen la administración de la secretaría corporativa de las sociedades a cargo. Supervisarás la administración y actualización permanente de los registros societarios de las subsidiarias mexicanas y extranjeras del grupo. Aprobarás y validarás la elaboración de documentos societarios, incluyendo actas de asamblea, actas de consejo de administración y libros corporativos. Asegurarás el cumplimiento de las obligaciones legales aplicables en materia societaria. Definirás y supervisarás los criterios para el otorgamiento y revocación de poderes. Mantendrás el control sobre las facultades conferidas para la correcta administración y funcionamiento de las sociedades del grupo. Liderarás la revisión y actualización de las políticas internas de delegación de facultades a funcionarios de la empresa. Fusiones, adquisiciones y desarrollo corporativo Liderarás y estructurarás proyectos de fusiones y adquisiciones, tanto internas como con terceros. Acompañarás proyectos estratégicos relacionados con el desarrollo corporativo del grupo. Trabajarás de manera conjunta con las áreas de Fiscal, Contraloría, Negocio, Ventas y Tesorería para definir estrategias relacionadas con posibles reestructuras corporativas. Analizarás y estructurarás los aspectos legales de operaciones corporativas complejas. Participarás en operaciones de mercado de capitales en México y en el extranjero. Coordinarás los aspectos legales relacionados con operaciones y proyectos internacionales y cross-border. Contratos, financiamiento y asuntos civiles y mercantiles Negociarás y aprobarás contratos en materia financiera, civil y mercantil. Participarás en la negociación y revisión de contratos relacionados con compraventa de acciones, préstamos y créditos, factoraje financiero, prestación de servicios, fideicomisos e inversiones, licencias y arrendamientos, entre otros. Brindarás asesoría legal estratégica a las áreas de Tesorería, Finanzas, Contraloría, Sourcing & Procurement, IT y Real Estate. Analizarás los riesgos e implicaciones legales de operaciones potenciales y proyectos estratégicos. Revisarás contratos con terceros, partes relacionadas y afiliadas necesarios para la operación diaria de la empresa. Asegurarás que las estructuras y documentos contractuales protejan adecuadamente los intereses del grupo. Gestionarás y coordinarás la relación con despachos externos cuando sea necesario. Liderazgo y gestión Liderarás, desarrollarás y acompañarás a abogados corporativos y/o paralegales. Supervisarás la correcta ejecución de las actividades y proyectos del equipo. Gestionarás prioridades y recursos para asegurar el cumplimiento oportuno de los compromisos del área. Proporcionarás asesoría y acompañamiento a líderes y stakeholders estratégicos de la organización. Participarás en la toma de decisiones relacionadas con asuntos corporativos y legales de alto impacto. Gestionarás la relación y coordinación con despachos externos y otros asesores especializados. Sobre ti Buscamos a un profesional con una sólida trayectoria en derecho corporativo, gobierno corporativo y operaciones estratégicas , con capacidad para liderar proyectos legales complejos y desenvolverse en un entorno corporativo dinámico y de alta exposición. Deberás contar con una visión estratégica y de negocio, así como con sólidas habilidades de negociación, comunicación y liderazgo. Esta posición requiere la capacidad de gestionar múltiples proyectos y prioridades simultáneamente, interactuar con diferentes niveles de la organización y proporcionar asesoría clara y estratégica para apoyar la toma de decisiones. Buscamos a alguien con capacidad para trabajar de manera autónoma, tomar decisiones bajo presión y construir relaciones sólidas con stakeholders internos y externos. Deberás tener Licenciatura en Derecho. Título y cédula profesional indispensables. Deseable maestría en Derecho Corporativo, Mercantil o un área afín. Experiencia mínima de 8 a 10 años en derecho corporativo, societario y fusiones y adquisiciones. Experiencia sólida en gobierno corporativo y administración societaria. Conocimiento profundo en derecho societario, notarial y gobierno corporativo. Experiencia en fusiones, adquisiciones y reestructuras corporativas. Conocimiento en mercado de capitales y financiamiento corporativo. Conocimiento sólido de derecho mercantil, civil y bancario. Deseable conocimiento del marco regulatorio de Estados Unidos aplicable a operaciones cross-border . Inglés avanzado. Experiencia en liderazgo, gestión y desarrollo de equipos de abogados y/o paralegales. Capacidad para comunicarse e interactuar con niveles ejecutivos y órganos de gobierno. Experiencia en la gestión y coordinación de despachos externos. Pensamiento estratégico y orientación al negocio. Sólidas habilidades de negociación y comunicación. Capacidad para tomar decisiones y gestionar prioridades bajo presión. Capacidad para trabajar de manera transversal con múltiples áreas y stakeholders. Beneficios En TelevisaUnivision ofrecemos la oportunidad de formar parte de una compañía líder en el mundo de los medios y el contenido en español, en un entorno dinámico, global y en constante evolución. Además, podrás disfrutar de beneficios competitivos y oportunidades de desarrollo profesional, colaborando con equipos multidisciplinarios y participando en proyectos estratégicos con impacto en la organización. Inclusión En TelevisaUnivision creemos que la diversidad y la inclusión fortalecen a nuestros equipos y nos permiten construir una organización más innovadora, creativa y representativa de las audiencias a las que servimos. Estamos comprometidos con brindar igualdad de oportunidades y construir un entorno de trabajo inclusivo, donde todas las personas puedan desarrollarse profesionalmente y aportar sus diferentes perspectivas, experiencias y talentos. job.title: Digital Account Manager
job.description: We are looking for a Digital Account manager to join our team! As an integral member of our team, you will partner with the Sales Account Executives from inception to execution of digital & cross platform ad campaigns that meet our clients’ objectives. Our team plays an essential role in driving ad sales revenue across our multimedia - digital, streaming, linear, social, experiential, and audio properties. You will collaborate with cross functional teams internally including planners, Operations, Marketing & Research. You will also work directly with clients to ensure the success of sponsorship programs and customized marketing initiatives. Coordinate all sponsorship executions across internal and external stakeholders. Develop strategic analysis and reporting during Upfront seasons and scatter markets Monitor all campaigns’ performance, and suggest improvements throughout the process Upsell clients on additional impressions and/or programs based on performance Partner with revenue management, inventory, research and analytics teams to create recap reports for key clients Collaborate with Ad Ops and trafficking teams to ensure flawless campaign launches and minimize setup issues. YOU HAVE: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience Minimum 2+ years of relevant experience with an agency, brand, and/or publisher Knowledge of advertising solutions across social, audio, display, streaming video, experiential and sports sponsorship platforms Must have knowledge and understanding of digital video and advanced audience targeting Proficiency in Excel and advanced data tools is a plus Must have knowledge and understanding of all client campaign strategies, brand messaging, and integration expectations Media math experience is preferred Strong problem-solving and reporting skills to address distribution, delivery, data and measurement needs Excellent presentation skills and ability to address both small and large groups. Please note the national salary range listed in the job posting reflects the new hire salary range across levels and U.S. locations that would be applicable to the position. job.title: Finance Manager, Digital, Record to Report
job.description: TelevisaUnivision is seeking a highly motivated Manager, Record to Report (Digital) to support the Digital Finance organization. This role is responsible for overseeing key accounting activities related to the monthly close process, general ledger management, account reconciliations, and financial reporting for the Digital business. The position partners closely with Digital Finance leadership to ensure accurate and timely financial results while driving process improvements, maintaining strong internal controls, and leading a team of accounting professionals. The position reports to the Vice President, Record to Report. ABOUT YOU: You are a collaborative and detail-oriented accounting professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment. You excel at managing competing priorities, solving complex problems, and partnering with leaders across the organization to deliver accurate financial results, strengthen internal controls, and drive continuous process improvements. You are an effective communicator and team player who can build strong relationships and lead accounting professionals to achieve shared goals. YOUR DAY-DAY: (aka Responsibilities) Financial Close and Reporting Oversee the monthly, quarterly, and annual close processes to ensure timely and accurate financial reporting. Review and approve journal entries, ensuring compliance with company accounting policies and close calendar deadlines. Review account reconciliations and ensure they are prepared, reviewed, and certified in accordance with company policies and internal control requirements. Prepare and review quarterly flux analysis packages, providing meaningful explanations of financial results and variances. Partner with the Digital CFO and Finance team to ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial statements. Accounting and General Ledger Management Manage day-to-day general ledger activities for the Digital business. Ensure compliance with U.S. GAAP, company accounting policies, and internal control requirements. Oversee accounting for specialized contractual arrangements and obligations. Review accounting treatment related to digital content licensing, produced content, programming rights, obligations, and related cash flow schedules. Interpret and analyze contracts to determine appropriate accounting treatment and financial impact. Lead Oracle ERP Record-to-Report processes, including financial consolidations, allocations, data interfaces, journal posting, period open/close activities, foreign currency exchange rate maintenance, revaluation and translation processes, cash management, subledger-to-ledger reconciliations, intercompany accounting, and governance of cross-validation rules to ensure accurate and compliant financial reporting. Team Leadership and Process Improvement Lead, develop, and mentor accounting staff, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Monitor team performance and service levels, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and effectiveness. Escalate significant issues, disputes, and risks to management in a timely manner. Maintain and enhance accounting procedures, process documentation, and internal controls. Collaborate with Enterprise Technology Services (ETS) and cross-functional stakeholders to identify and implement process and system improvements. Audit and Compliance Coordinate and support internal and external audit requests, ensuring timely delivery of required documentation and analysis. Assist in maintaining compliance with SOX and internal control requirements. Ensure supporting documentation is complete, accurate, and audit-ready. Projects and Initiatives Support system implementations, integrations, and other finance transformation initiatives. Participate in special projects and ad hoc analyses as requested by Finance leadership. Drive automation and standardization efforts to improve the efficiency of Record-to-Report processes. YOU HAVE: (aka Qualifications) Bachelor’s degree in accounting 5+ yrs. accounting experience Strong PC Skills with moderate knowledge of Excel Certified Public Accountant is a plus Ability to speak/write/understand Spanish is preferred. Ability to work flexible hours, as there will be work weeks that require more than 40 hours to ensure the Company’s reporting requirements are met. OUR BENEFITS: TelevisaUnivision believes that a happy, well-balanced employee is what makes our culture thrive. We offer a wide selection of perks and benefits including PTO; tuition reimbursement; wellness and employee support programs; 401K; and life and other insurance plans. job.description: The Legal Department at TelevisaUnivision is looking for a Senior Director of Legal Operations to join our team! The Senior Director of Legal Operations is the operational, technical and business management leader for the Legal department, partnering with Legal leadership to establish and execute the department’s operating strategy and drive efficiency, scalability, financial discipline and continuous improvement. In this position you will help develop, refine and promote the legal department’s short and long-term operations plan, including managing law firm and third-party vendor management programs, optimizing financial resources leveraging technology and supporting the development and implementation of a sound annual plan. The role will report to the SVP, Chief Privacy Officer and Head of Legal Operations, and will serve as key business partner to Legal team leadership. This position will interface with Finance, HR and other cross-functional partners across the team and company to drive meaningful operational improvements. ABOUT YOU: You are a strategic Legal Operations leader who combines strong business acumen with deep operational and technical expertise. You are comfortable navigating complex organizations, independently identifying opportunities for improvement, and translating strategy into practical execution. You bring strong project and relationship management skills and have a demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders at all levels, manage complex initiatives, negotiate with external partners, and build scalable processes. You are data- and technology-savvy, curious about emerging AI capabilities, and able to identify where technology can meaningfully improve the effectiveness and efficiency of a Legal department. YOUR DAY-DAY: (aka Responsibilities) Strategic Planning & Execution Provide creative thinking to help identify and develop cutting-edge strategies for increasing value and reducing outside legal spend, while maintaining excellent legal representation and optimizing engagement practices with our law firms. Manage other strategic plans or initiatives to make the legal department more efficient, as delegated by the SVP, Chief Privacy Officer and Head of Legal Operations, and other Legal team leadership. Create metrics and monitor progress to measure success against strategic plans. Benchmark both internally and externally to stay on top of current trends and emerging and best practices and opportunities to improve the team’s operating model and performance. Finance and Budget Management Partner with Legal leadership, finance and procurement to develop and manage the legal annual operating plan and all department budgets. Work as primary interface between the legal department and finance. Identify, collect, and report on key performance indicators and metrics on a global basis that are meaningful and relevant in ascertaining the legal team’s budget management performance, including spend analysis, efficiency initiatives and technology. Manage and develop Billing Supervisor and oversee Legal billing operations and related processes. Legal Information Technology and Artificial Intelligence Lead the Legal department’s technology and AI strategy, identifying opportunities to leverage existing and emerging technologies to improve productivity, automate processes, enhance knowledge management, reduce costs and mitigate risks. Assess and implement technology (e.g., matter management, knowledge management, Evisort, ethics and compliance, document management, electronic billing and compliance systems), including tools with AI-enable functionality, to streamline operations, improve cost effectiveness and implement best in class systems and processes. Lead continuous process improvement initiatives and work with IT on automation as needed. Work closely with selected electronic billing provider to implement system enhancements, run detailed reports within the software tool and create spend dashboards. Outside Counsel and Legal Vendor Management Update and manage master retention agreements, billing guidelines, and pricing models for outside counsel. Develop tracking and reporting systems to monitor pricing performance and savings across engagements. Manage relationships with outside counsel and vendors, including conducting RFPs and negotiating fee arrangements. Communications & Administration Align legal workflows with department priorities to increase efficiency, leveraging technology. Manage new hire onboarding in collaboration with HR, training, and policy implementation for the legal team. Collaborate with HR, IT, and other departments on company-wide initiatives. Talent Management and Education Track and maintain records for Continuing Legal Education (CLE) requirements for all lawyers Manage and provide regular CLE programming, both live and asynchronously, for Department lawyers. YOU HAVE: (aka Qualifications) Bachelor’s Degree preferably in Business, Finance or equivalent combination of education and professional experience. 15 plus years of total work experience in operations or law firm management, ten years in legal operations. Demonstrated experience developing and executing strategic and operational plans and delivering measurable improvements in efficiency, cost, quality, and service. In-depth understanding of law firm billing, pricing and compensation practices Demonstrated experience with alternative fee arrangement cost modeling At least two years' experience evaluating, implementing and using legal technology, automation, and AI-enabled solutions (including contract lifecycle management, electronic billing and ediscovery), with a demonstrated ability to translate technology capabilities into meaningful business improvements and cost efficiencies. Technology- and AI-savvy; proficient in all Microsoft Office applications, especially Excel; expertise with electronic billing and contract management software. job.title: Ad Solutions & Campaign Management Intern
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

Job Description

The New York Times' Advertising team is looking for an Ads Solutions and Campaign Management Intern to join the team. As an Ads Solutions and Campaign Management intern, you will support the post-sale creative production, trafficking, delivery and reporting of digital campaigns across The New York Times portfolio. You will work closely with Campaign Managers and Producers to ensure that advertiser creatives align with client expectations and that campaigns are set up accurately, deliver on schedule and meet our quality standards.


About The Role

This internship is an opportunity to gain hands-on experience and training in digital creative production and ad operations within a global, premium publisher environment. This is a hybrid role based in our Paris headquarters, reporting to the Director, Ad Solutions & Operations. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week. The position will start from September for a duration of 6 months, based in Paris. Candidates must have the right to work in France for the full duration of the internship.

  • This internship is intended for students or recent graduates who meet the legal requirements for an internship (stage) in France with a mandatory “Convention de stage”.
  • To apply, please submit:
    • Your CV
    • A short cover letter explaining your interest in digital advertising and this specific role

Responsibilities:

  • Support Ad Solutions in the creative production process:
    • Helping compile specs and example executions for clients based on signed media plans
    • Reviewing assets for technical specification compliancy
    • Customising units according to client guidelines using CSS3
    • Testing ads across browsers, screen sizes and devices
  • Support Campaign Managers with the end-to-end setup of digital campaigns, including:
    • Collecting and validating creative assets and tracking tags
    • Trafficking campaigns in GAM, AdSwizz and LiveIntent
  • Assist in monitoring live campaigns:
    • Reviewing pacing and delivery reports
    • Flagging under-delivery or issues to the Campaign Manager in a timely manner
    • Supporting optimisations based on performance and client objectives
  • Contribute to campaign reporting:
    • Pulling performance data from ad servers and other platforms
    • Assisting in the preparation of client-facing reports and post-campaign summaries
  • Support day-to-day operations:
    • Collaborating with Sales, Planning and other internal stakeholders on campaign-related tasks
    • Maintaining internal dashboards and trackers as required
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Interest in digital advertising
  • Experience working with numbers and spreadsheets (e.g. basic formulas, filtering and pivot tables in Excel/Google Sheets)
  • Experience with a detailed and structured working style
  • Experience prioritizing competing programs, responsibilities, and projects
  • Professional proficiency in English

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Basic understanding of digital advertising concepts (impressions, clicks, CTR, viewability, targeting, etc.)
  • Familiarity with HTML5, CSS3 and JS.
  • Exposure to or interest in ad serving, analytics or marketing platforms (e.g. Google Ad Manager, campaign management tools, web analytics)
  • Experience working with datasets, reporting or dashboards (e.g. coursework, projects, part-time roles)
  • Previous internship or work experience in media, advertising, marketing or a related field
  • Professional proficiency in French

REQ-020595

Additional Compensation and Benefits

For roles in the U.S., dependent on your role, you may be eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. Benefits may include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs.

For roles outside of the U.S., information on benefits will be provided during the interview process.

job.description:

Job Description

The New York Times Advertising is hiring for an Art Director to join our T Brand Studio. As an Art Director, you will lead the visual execution of assigned projects. Art Directors do the following: they imagine ways to tell stories visually. They present visual ideas and recommendations internally and to our clients. They find visual reference, specifically relevant to each idea, project, and opportunity. They contribute to and oversee the creation of great mood boards, inspired type treatments, exceptional color palettes, and page layouts.

About the Role

You will oversee the design of presentations which enhance our work, the assembly of excellent paid posts in webflow, the design of impactful print ads, and work with developers internal and external on complex custom projects. You will mentor Designers and Senior Designers, and collaborate with external partners, building relationships and guiding them through insightful feedback to create their best work. This is a hybrid role, reporting to the Director, Design. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Contribute to and oversee excellent design work on client and internal projects, with guidance from Design Directors, and Creative Directors.
  • Translate conceptual and strategic ideas into impactful visual solutions.
  • Contribute creative concepts to client and internal projects, brainstorming with other teams.
  • Design iteratively with an easy command of typography, composition, messaging hierarchy, layout, and other fundamental principles of graphic design, and give pointed feedback to designers which directly improves their work.
  • Research and oversee selection of visual reference that inspires (Design, Page Animation, Illustration, and Photography), and build a mental reference library of styles, approaches, creators, and projects.
  • Manage Designers, delegate work to resourced Designers and Senior Designers based on workload, capabilities, and experience. Contribute to the professional growth of direct reports through mentorship, and feedback.
  • Select, brief, and direct outside collaborators to create their best work.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of professional work experience in the art industry
  • 5+ years of experience with Adobe Creative Cloud (InDesign, Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma) and modern digital publishing platforms such as Webflow.
  • An experienced creative portfolio demonstrating mastery of design principles - specifically typography, grid systems, layout hierarchy, color theory, and art direction for both digital and print media
  • Experienced managing designers including delegating tasks, giving constructive feedback, and overseeing visual quality.
  • Experience commissioning and directing external creative partners including photographers, illustrators, animators and external development teams
  • Experience presenting visual strategies and creative direction to executive-level clients and company partners.
  • Visual research skills, with a rich, active mental library of contemporary and historical art, design, photography, and interactive digital trends.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Working knowledge of front-end web technologies (HTML/CSS) and an understanding of dynamic layout capabilities, responsive design, and digital motion/animation principles.
  • Experience in luxury, editorial, or prestige brand storytelling, with a deep appreciation for high-end aesthetic stewardship and cultural context.
  • Experience prioritizing competing programs, responsibilities, and projects
  • Experience working in a collaborative design space/team

Partnering closely with Opinion Print Editors, you will reimagine our daily pages to establish a distinct visual identity separate from the newsroom. You will demonstrate your talent to organize complex information and create engaging designs. As a story-first editorial partner, you will combine sophisticated typography, photography, data visualization, and commissioned artwork, or create real-time illustration when needed, to push the boundaries of print layouts. You are passionate about print and interested in generating innovative ways to present and adapt digital-first content. You will bring advanced editorial design experience, strong project management skills to support daily deadline pressure, a deep passion for journalism, and a portfolio demonstrating versatile, high-impact narrative storytelling.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

  • Conceptualize and execute design solutions from initial concept through publication across print and digital platforms

  • Push layout boundaries through sophisticated art placement, structure, and illustration integration

  • Manage full project lifecycles within proprietary publishing systems, meeting tight daily deadlines in a fast-paced constantly evolving news environment

  • Proven art direction and visual editing skills, including commissioning talent, curating photo assets, and illustrating directly under tight timelines
  • Mastery of design tools (Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, pagination software) and pre-press production, including color correction and print-ready prep

job.title: Assistant Editor, Fine Arts
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

The New York Times Culture desk covers the arts and culture to help people understand the world. Through our reporting, criticism and service journalism, we provide trusted guidance to help people live fuller, more considered lives.

We are seeking an Assistant Editor, Fine Arts to help shape and elevate our coverage of visual art, architecture and design; museums and other art institutions; and auctions, with an eye toward ambitious, distinctive journalism that reaches a broad, curious audience. You should have expertise that will produce stories that lead readers into the boardrooms and the studios of today's cultural influencers and will also develop stories about the intersection of art and new media, including artificial intelligence.

You will work closely with the art discipline editor, critics and reporters to determine coverage, assign, edit and second edit news, features, reviews and visual story forms.

You'll also manage a critic and assign and oversee the work of freelancers. You should have a deep understanding of fine arts and art institutions, strong editing skills across formats and platforms and a track record of guiding world-class journalism.

This is a hybrid position, based in New York City, and includes regular attendance in the office at least four days each week.

Responsibilities:

  • Help identify and prioritize key fine-arts storylines, from breaking news to longer-term investigations, profiles and criticism that illuminate how the arts intersect with politics, power and the broader culture
  • Assign, shape and edit daily art stories, including news, features, criticism, service pieces, visual pieces and enterprise projects
  • Assign and edit news of institutions, including museums, art galleries, auction houses and non-profits, throughout the U.S. and Europe
  • Respond to news events in the art world by assigning and editing timely stories, explainers and off-the-news pieces that give readers essential context and insight
  • Plan and assign advance obituary coverage of notables in art
  • Coordinate with our European cultural editor on coverage of major events including biennales and museum openings
  • Manage and direct the work of at least one critic
  • Assign, schedule and edit freelance reviews for Weekend Arts, including the weekly Galleries section
  • Identify and shape features and profiles for the weekly Arts & Leisure page
  • Collaborate with photo, design, visual and video editors on stories across a variety of formats
  • Help foster a collaborative, inclusive culture on the desk, modeling clear communication, constructive feedback and high editorial standards
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Art Editor

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7–10 years of editing experience, ideally as an editor in a newsroom
  • Knowledge of and curiosity about visual art
  • A track record of editing a variety of story forms and formats
  • Ability to meet deadlines, juggle multiple stories at once and make sound editorial decisions under pressure
  • Excellent communication and organizational skills, including the ability to manage complex workflows and coordinate across multiple teams

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supervising or mentoring journalists, including guiding reporters from pitch through publication
  • Experience working closely with visual, audio and video teams on digital storytelling, and a willingness to experiment with new formats
  • Familiarity with Times style, standards and journalistic independence, and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • A demonstrated ability to collaborate across desks and disciplines, building strong working relationships in a large, complex newsroom
  • A passion for expanding the audience for arts coverage and making our journalism accessible, surprising and indispensable to a global readership

job.description:

The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. In service of that mission, we have a journalism operation that includes thousands of people reporting on the ground from most countries around the world, producing journalism with the independence, accuracy, depth and authority for which The Times is famous.

Marketing plays a key part in extending this journalistic legacy into the future. Our job is to answer the question, “Why is quality journalism worth paying for?” We create award-winning marketing that builds our brand and deepens affinity for our journalistic offering. Above all, we strive to be timely, straightforward and relevant — illustrating in new and creative ways how The New York Times can enrich the lives of our readers.

We are seeking an Associate Creative Director, Earned Activations (Contract) to lead the creative vision for our specific “earned” marketing initiatives. This is a critical leadership role for a creative strategist who can move beyond traditional advertising to produce culturally resonant work that drives organic press and social conversation.

Reporting to the Creative Director, Design, with a dotted line to the Executive Director, Brand Marketing, you will serve as a creative partner to our marketing, editorial, comms, commerce, photo, external agency partners, Games and The Athletic creative teams. You will be responsible for dreaming up and executing ideas that turn the value of our world-class journalism and lifestyle products into shareable experiences. You will focus exclusively on creating a cohesive but distinct earned lens for our core products: News, The Athletic, Games, and Cooking.

We will look to you to bring unexpected, deeply resonant thinking to how we market our journalism, championing creative ideas that can break through the noise of the modern media landscape.

This is a temporary hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters, reporting to the the Creative Director, Design. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Concept and lead the development of brand-building activations, partnerships, and communications content designed specifically to generate earned media and social sharing.

  • Direct the day-to-day work of a Senior Designer, Earned providing clear conceptual vision to guide projects from strategy to launch. You will oversee the translation of earned media concepts into high-quality design solutions, ensuring that every deliverable—from seeding kits to social assets—upholds The New York Times's rigorous brand standards.

  • Translate marketing strategies into clear, provocative creative directives that excite internal teams and external partners.

  • Develop creative ideas tailored to the unique audiences of our core products, ensuring a cohesive visual and conceptual narrative for News, The Athletic, Games, and Cooking.

  • Create work that natively integrates celebrities, influencers, and culturally noteworthy subscribers to amplify our mission in ways that feel authentic and newsworthy.

  • Guide the creation of "social-first" activations designed to thrive on digital platforms and spark community engagement without relying solely on paid media or editorially motivated social media handles.

  • In partnership with the Director, Creative Strategy and Earned Production and Director, Brand Earned Activations, guide external agency relationships to ensure top-notch quality and brand/product standards are enforced.

  • Work closely with the Executive Director of Brand Activations and Talent to ensure earned ideas align with broader business goals.

  • Act as an ambassador for earned thinking across the organization, engaging the right stakeholders in productive conversations to build alignment.

  • Execute high-concept ideas, balancing quality with the demands of the news cycle.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • 8+ years of experience in creative leadership, with a heavy focus on earned media, PR-led activations, or non-traditional advertising.

  • A portfolio that demonstrates “work the world talked about”—campaigns that broke through via PR, social trends, or cultural moments.

  • Deep understanding of how to leverage Social, Celebrity, and Influencer ecosystems to drive brand discovery.

  • Experience translating marketing strategies, product roadmaps, and the news cycle into clear creative directives.

job.title: Associate Creative Director, Events
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

The New York Times creates original, quality journalism in many forms, from the daily paper to The Daily podcast. Our live events play an important role in this mission, connecting readers to the story and to each other. From flagship convenings like DealBook and Climate Forward to immersive gatherings like Hard Fork Live, New York Times events intrigue, inform and inspire in equal measure.

This is a leadership role for an accomplished creative who can translate the value of world-class journalism into powerful design experiences. You will help bring New York Times journalism to life and create compelling environments for a portfolio of public events and experiences. You will lead creative work that defines both individual events and the overall audience experience across our events portfolio. As part of a cross-disciplinary team, you will shape how audiences experience these moments across every touchpoint, from physical stages to digital screens to marketing assets.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters and requires regular in-office attendance three days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the strategic visual development and art direction for our portfolio of public events and experiences, demonstrating expert knowledge of spatial design, environmental graphics, wayfinding, audience journeys, live audience engagement, and meticulous physical execution.
  • Guide the creative lifecycle of each event—from naming and foundational identity to marketing campaigns, live production, and post-event storytelling.
  • Thoughtfully integrate the design of sponsor support into revenue-generating events, balancing business objectives with an audience experience that reflects the values of our journalism.
  • Art direct video interstitials and live screen graphics, working closely with our Senior Writer for Events to merge narrative outlines with visual storytelling, and collaborating with editors and motion designers to create work that defines the event experience.
  • Work across editorial, events, and marketing to secure resources, navigate live-event production challenges, and steward relationships between editorial priorities and advertising objectives.
  • Oversee the thoughtful documentation of our events, working with photo editors to capture high-quality visual assets that extend the life of the experience and support future programming and partnerships.
  • Manage and mentor a design team dedicated to event projects, cultivating an environment of high-quality execution, continuous learning, and diverse perspectives.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Creative Director for Culture, Communications and Live Experience.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of hands-on experience in brand identity, spatial and experiential design, environmental graphics, and live-event production.
  • Experience designing for physical environments, including signage systems, audience wayfinding, and large-scale event graphics.
  • A versatile design portfolio showcasing an experience with layout, typography, and experience handling high-profile editorial content and designing around newsmakers.
  • A strong conceptual understanding of motion design and the ability to think in and direct motion, with considerable experience collaborating with external motion design studios or internal teams to execute graphics for event screens, presentations, and digital platforms.
  • Familiarity with video production workflows and experience directing editors, motion designers, and video teams on larger-scale event productions.
  • Proficiency across contemporary design tools (Figma, Adobe Creative Suite) and presentation software (Google Slides), with a strong understanding of motion workflows and social publishing platforms.
  • B.A., B.S., B.F.A. or M.F.A.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A track record of effective people management, including creating robust development plans, delivering actionable feedback, and fostering an environment of trust and respect.
  • A high bar of accountability and the ability to navigate the demands of live-event production under tight deadlines.
  • A genuine passion for journalism and a deep curiosity about our work and company—we hope you enjoy reading, watching, and listening to it.

Job Description

The New York Times Advertising is hiring an Associate Programmatic Sales Director to join our Sales Team. You will join The Times at a very exciting time, as we tap into the enormous programmatic demand for quality audiences and content from our agency and advertiser partners. Success will require an intensity of effort, demonstrated through targeted outreach, pitch meetings, and securing new PMP deals, in partnership with The Times's vertical sales teams. This is a temp position, beginning mid-October, 2026, covering the Programmatic Sales Director.

About the Role

You will grow our programmatic revenue across The New York Times portfolio. Using existing programmatic-buyer relationships is an imperative for success. You will engage with Ad Monetization, Ad Product, and Product Marketing teams to grow our programmatic value proposition and capability awareness in-market. This is a hybrid role, reporting to the VP, Head of Agency Development and Sales Strategy. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Programmatic Sales Strategy: Develop and execute a plan to secure programmatic deals from PMP spenders who are active in the market along with NYTA-direct accounts, in collaboration with the direct sales team.
  • Full-Funnel Accountability involves overseeing client relationships and revenue outcomes. This oversight occurs before and after PMP creation. To meet client commitments and identify growth opportunities, one must work with Account Management, Ad Operations, and Direct Sales.
  • Industry Expert: You understand agency programmatic needs, determine what KPI's are required for successful PMP outcomes, and recognize how you impact new and prospective advertisers with the NYT audience.
  • Sales Collaboration: Champion all programmatic-related efforts across the sales organization by being the PMP expert for direct sales. This includes leading post-sale account management collaboration and external client engagements.
  • Buyer Relationships: Establish and maintain relationships with agency and advertiser buyers, understanding their marketing goals and applying our suite of programmatic products.
  • Prospecting: Understanding of where programmatic spend is happening in the market and create conversations with net-new NYTA advertisers
  • Tech-Stack Mastery: Understand The New York Times technology stack, to be the first line of defense in supporting troubleshooting deals and addressing obstacles with clients
  • Voice of the Buyer: Represent buyer needs to guide Ad Product roadmap and Product Marketing collateral toward agreement on external demand
  • Campaign Optimization: Collaborate with our teams to ensure campaigns are driving maximum revenue
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years experience of the programmatic advertising ecosystem.
  • 2+ years experience programmatic sales
  • Experience meeting sales goals, with a history of building and nurturing high-value programmatic-buyer relationships within the digital media space.
  • Experience applying data to inform strategic decisions, forecast trends, and optimize campaign performance
  • Experience explaining complex programmatic concepts in a clear manner to diverse audiences
  • Experience operating in ambiguity and strategies to keep pace with industry developments.

  • Publisher experience

job.title: Audience Editor, NYT Wirecutter
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

Wirecutter is seeking an editor to lead programming and personalization for our ecommerce initiatives, with a particular emphasis on the Wirecutter Store. You will be the editorial lead for how we talk about the Store — crafting language, frameworks, and campaigns that invite readers in, explain what the Store is, and bring them back during major editorial moments throughout the year.

As audience editor for ecommerce, programming, and personalization, you will focus on three core areas: messaging, copy, and alignment with stakeholders around big editorial moments; audience strategy, lifecycle flows, and personalization rooted in our standards; and editorial programming and email support that tightly links our journalism to new platforms.

As an audience editor, you will report to Wirecutter's deputy director of newsletters and programming, and collaborate closely with colleagues across newsletters and programming, audience at large, Wirecutter's newsroom, as well as our commerce, marketing, product, and analytics teams.

You will drive the editorial voice of Store-related messaging, build and maintain a unified promo calendar, and design tests and experiments to deepen engagement while valuing Wirecutter's standards for independence and trust.

You'll bring thoughtful editorial judgment, comfort working with data, and a sense of how lifecycle messaging, personalization, and on-site experiences can work together to serve readers.

This role has the potential to be remote, though New York City–based applicants are preferred.

Responsibilities:

  • Drive the voice and editorial quality of Wirecutter Store-related messaging across channels: Write and line-edit copy for newsletters, lifecycle flows, push, SMS, on-site promos, and Wirecutter Store entry points with deep editorial rigor and collaboration across partner teams.
  • Support the editorial quality of product detail pages (PDPs) on the Wirecutter Store:
  • Create messaging frameworks for major Store moments (launches, tentpoles, seasonal pushes) so readers understand what the Store is and why they should trust it.
  • Partner with marketing to ensure users are engaged at every touchpoint in the lifecycle, from acquisition campaigns to transactional emails and targeted promos.
  • Create and maintain a Store messaging style guide that aligns with Wirecutter's voice and company-wide Store goals, including guidelines for CTAs, subject lines, and promotional framing.
  • Contribute to overall Wirecutter newsletters and programming responsibilities — especially during major moments where it connects to the Store (i.e. gifting season; deal events).
  • Work closely with product and data to understand how we are engaging readers across surfaces, and design editorial experiments to better reach and engage with them based on behaviors — particularly in inboxes
  • Continuously test and optimize messaging (subject lines, CTAs, timing, sequencing) to improve engagement while staying rooted in our standards and reporting.
  • Maintain a unified Store messaging and promo calendar that's integrated with Wirecutter's broader editorial, promotional, and major deal events strategy, rather than running on a separate track.
  • Work closely with edit leadership and in collaboration with cross-functional teams like marketing and product to design reader journeys that connect journalism to the Store to follow-ups in a way that feels personal, useful, and closely connected to overall editorial reader journeys.
  • Perform related work as assigned.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Deputy Director, Newsletters and Programming, NYT Wirecutter.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years in a newsroom, audience, or editorial marketing role with substantial experience in writing, editing, or programming for digital audiences.
  • Demonstrated experience with email newsletters, lifecycle or CRM programs, or other audience-led messaging channels; familiarity with ecommerce or product-focused journalism.
  • Excellent editorial judgment, line-editing skills, and a strong sense of how to translate rigorous reporting into clear, compelling, and trustworthy copy.
  • Proven ability to use analytics, A/B testing, and audience insights to inform messaging decisions and iterate on subject lines, CTAs, timing, and personalization.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Comfort working cross-functionally with product, marketing, commerce, data, and creative partners, and an ability to advocate for reader-first, journalism-informed decisions.
  • Strong organizational and project-management skills, including experience maintaining calendars, managing complex campaigns, and keeping multiple stakeholders aligned.
  • A deep interest in Wirecutter's mission and a commitment to upholding our standards for independence, rigor, and service journalism in all Store-related communications.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

This role will lead the rollout and growth of both our YouTube-first video shows and audio shows, ensuring they are published and packaged effectively while monitoring how they perform over time. Strategic work includes: analyzing performance data, highlighting wins and areas for improvement, and surfacing competitive insights that inform future packaging and rollout. We’re looking for someone eager to execute and report on performance, with a strong understanding of YouTube and other social video platforms.

We are looking for someone with a proven track record of driving video engagement and reach, and who is eager to refine and expand our distribution strategies to maximize the reach and impact of Times video shows.

job.title: Business Correspondent, Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

The New York Times is looking for a talented, experienced and versatile correspondent to join the tech pod on the Business desk to cover Elon Musk's artificial intelligence work. Musk, a founder of OpenAI, has long been invested in the technology and its implications. He is making A.I. central to SpaceX and Tesla, his two main companies, and is competing with other Silicon Valley titans in dealmaking, geopolitics, national security, and financing of the technology.

We are looking for an energetic, determined and collegial journalist who thrives when competing on the most compelling and important storylines. Proven success in building and cultivating sources and experience reporting on companies are prerequisites. You will work closely with other tech reporters in the United States and around the world. This is a high metabolism job, with breaking news, second-day stories, analysis, explainers, profiles, accountability stories and enterprise. You will collaborate across multiple desks and teams including finance, Audio, Video and Graphics. You will write articles, short Live updates, contribute to newsletters and videos and participate in collaborative reporting projects.

This is an in-office position, based in San Francisco and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • You will generate original reporting on news, events and trends on Musk and his A.I. efforts, in conjunction with your colleagues and editors, themes worthy of coverage as breaking news, day news or as enterprise.

  • You will build a network of sources that will inform rich and original reports, news and features.

  • You will write with authority, clarity, and independently.

  • You must be as comfortable and enthusiastic handling breaking news as you are writing thoughtfully and deeply about events, issues, finances and people.

  • You will write medium- and long-term enterprise and the occasional entertaining feature.

  • You will cover news accurately and efficiently; maintain and cultivate news sources and contacts; obtain information through interviews, observations and research.

  • You will present facts and analysis in clear written form and in conformity with Times style, length and other requirements, and developing high-impact stories from the broader themes that underpin incremental news developments.

  • You will write on deadline; receive and react to feedback and edits.

  • You will contribute to and sometimes be the lead correspondent on live briefings, join planning meetings and provide live coverage.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Business Tech Editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of significant beat reporting and writing experience.

  • Demonstrated ability to produce stories that are crisply written and well organized, framed to draw in busy, scrolling readers and delivered in language that is accessible.

  • Experience as a collaborator and the ability to partner with colleagues across The New York Times newsroom.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A passion for professional development and the ability to learn from everyone around them.

  • A collaborative, genuine and independent spirit that takes satisfaction in not only their own growth but the success of their team and colleagues.

  • Interest in directly engaging with our audiences to deepen their relationships with The Times.

  • A willingness to be flexible as the newsroom's needs evolve.

  • A bottomless curiosity about the world and a love of news and storytelling.

  • A commitment to the power of tough and fair reporting.

To be considered for this role, please submit your resume and cover letter, including links to 5-7 clips that demonstrate your range.

job.description:

About the Role

The state of the global economy. The emergence of artificial intelligence. The rapidly changing media and entertainment ecosystems. The New York Times’s business desk is on the forefront of some of the biggest issues of our times, serving a general interest audience but also closely watched by many of the influential powerbrokers we cover.

We are seeking a dynamic journalist to lead our business desk — both to uphold its strong foundation and to lead its evolution in a relentlessly shifting news and media environment.

The successful candidate ought to have a strong news metabolism and a record of motivating reporters to break consequential stories and produce competitive coverage, including explanatory, analytical and investigative journalism. You are steeped in business coverage and have an innovative vision for making our report even more essential, from the conception of beats to the use of new storytelling forms. You are an experienced manager who can oversee and coordinate the work of large teams of journalists, while collaborating effectively with departments across a large newsroom.

You will oversee a report expressed across multiple formats: text, video, photo, interactive graphics, and more. And you are attuned to maintaining a healthy culture that fosters teamwork, high morale and professional development for a large global staff.

This position is based in our New York City headquarters. It is a full-time role that includes regular attendance in the office each week. It reports to Carolyn Ryan, managing editor

Responsibilities

  • Lead the Business report of The New York Times, including driving competitive news coverage, generating scoops and ambitious enterprise, incorporating visual and other forms into the report, and setting desk goals and overseeing performance
  • Develop and uphold a strong and cohesive workplace culture
  • Collaborate with colleagues on desks across the newsroom
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience as an editor
  • 5+ years in a significant leadership or managerial role within a major media organization
  • Experience assigning stories and directing coverage
  • Track record of producing varied storyforms
  • Strong news judgment
  • Demonstrated exceptional editing skills, with the ability to sharpen complex critiques, elevate prose, and guide writers toward their best work under tight deadlines.
  • Experience successfully navigating complex, matrixed organizational structures.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience

job.description:

And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

The Audience Manager is an exciting role within T Brand Studio, the award-winning content studio of The New York Times Advertising department. Inspired by the journalism, creativity and innovation of The New York Times newsroom, the team partners with brands to tell meaningful stories that resonate with our global audience and create lasting impact.

Based in London, this role leads the end-to-end management of branded content distribution campaigns across The New York Times' on-site and off-site channels, developing audience strategies and driving campaign optimisation and measurement. Working closely with creative, strategy, sales and media planning teams across London, Paris, Singapore and New York, the Audience Manager helps deliver exceptional campaign performance while contributing to the ongoing evolution of our distribution and measurement capabilities.

This is a key client-facing role, partnering directly with agencies and brands to communicate campaign performance, audience insights and business impact. The successful candidate will confidently translate data into compelling stories while building trusted client relationships.

The role requires a strong understanding of the evolving media landscape across social, video, audio and editorial formats, alongside a forward-looking mindset that identifies opportunities to enhance our distribution, measurement and optimisation capabilities through new technologies, vendor partnerships and best practices.

The role will report directly to the Associate Director of Audience Development & Insights based in London as part of the broader T Brand Strategy Team.

Responsibilities

  • Schedule, manage and optimise distribution campaigns across The New York Times' on-site native placements, social media channels and third-party distribution networks.
  • Develop weekly and end-of-campaign performance reports that translate campaign metrics into actionable insights for clients and internal stakeholders.
  • Advise editorial, production and design teams on branded content best practices, new formats and distribution strategies.
  • Partner with sales, strategy and creative teams during pre-sale to support pitches with audience insights, best practices and performance benchmarks.
  • Manage multiple campaigns simultaneously while collaborating with cross-functional teams across international markets.
  • Research audience behaviour, advertising trends and the competitive landscape to inform campaign strategy and identify new opportunities.
  • Share campaign learnings and best practices to continually improve creative performance.
  • Support the development and delivery of campaign effectiveness and brand measurement solutions, including brand lift studies and attention-based methodologies.
  • Evaluate emerging measurement tools and vendor partnerships to expand T Brand Studio International's measurement capabilities.
  • Collaborate with internal teams and external partners to test and scale new measurement frameworks that demonstrate business outcomes beyond traditional engagement metrics.

Basic Qualifications

  • Campaign management experience using tools such as Google ads manager, Pressboard, Social Media advertising (Facebook, Instagram, Youtube, Tiktok)
  • Experience with data analysis and storytelling, going beyond the “what” to tell the “why” within research results
  • Experience managing stakeholders in a client facing role
  • Capable of handling multiple projects in a fast paced, deadline driven environment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of media tools, data and audience measurement tools (MRI, Ipsos Affluent Survey, GWI, SimilarWeb or Google Analytics etc.)

job.title: China Correspondent
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

The New York Times is looking for an experienced journalist to cover China.

China’s transformation to geopolitical and economic colossus over the past several decades has bolstered its confidence at home and its influence abroad. Beijing has leveraged its might, both commercially and militarily, to redraw the terms of trade, security and diplomacy. Under Xi Jinping’s leadership, China has sought to offer a model of governance that challenges the liberal democratic order and the dominance of the United States.

China is one of the biggest stories we cover, and one of the most challenging. It’s also one of the most exciting, a constantly changing and diverse country with few parallels on the planet. It touches nearly every major issue. Geopolitics. Demographics. Inequality. Climate Change. Trade. Technology.

The role requires a strong writer with the ability to juggle breaking news, smart analysis and ambitious enterprise. We want someone eager to react quickly to news as necessary, but who is also able to write thoughtfully and deeply about important issues and events. We are looking for an entrepreneurial correspondent who can embrace the multitudes, to cover the news and the nuance.

This position will be based in Beijing, China, or elsewhere in Asia.

Main responsibilities:

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our values of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • Deliver timely coverage of major breaking news events about China and its influence in the region, providing clarity, accuracy, and sharp analytical context for a global audience.
  • Conceive, pitch, and execute ambitious enterprise stories and deeply reported features that reveal the nuances of political, societal and demographic shifts, economic inequality, and cultural trends.
  • Track and analyze China’s expanding global footprint, reporting on how Beijing leverages its commercial, technological, and military might to reshape international trade, climate policy, and global diplomacy.
  • Cultivate and maintain a diverse and robust network of sources— including policymakers, businesspeople, scholars, commentators and ordinary citizens—while navigating a highly restrictive and complex reporting environment with resilience and integrity.
  • Collaborate across formats, partnering closely with Photo, Video, Audio and Graphics teams to produce visually rich, immersive journalism that elevates our storytelling.
  • Work collegially with the broader China bureau and regional editors in Asia, as well as the broader international desk.

Qualifications:

  • Deep international reporting experience, preferably for a global news organization.
  • Experience working in China and/or fluency in Mandarin.
  • A keen eye for news and other great stories, borne of experience reporting and writing.
  • Eagerness to collaborate with colleagues across Photo, Video, Audio and other departments to bring stories to life in a variety of formats.
  • A constant drive to develop and maintain new sources, and a commitment to fairness and independence in reporting and presentation.
  • Commitment to The New York Times’s standards and mission.

In order to be considered for this role, please submit your resume, a PDF/link of your top 5-7 clips, and a coverage memo laying out the themes and some specific stories you would want to take on.

job.title: China Correspondent, Science
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

The Science desk of the New York Times is looking for a creative, energetic reporter to cover Chinese science for an English-speaking audience. We’re looking for someone who can read widely, in Mandarin and/or Cantonese, and English, and develop a large and diverse network of sources in order to find stories that dramatize the precipitous rise of China as a scientific powerhouse. Topics will include major investments and funding cuts, rising and falling academic stars, the personalities and narratives behind pathbreaking research, the rise of A.I., and more.

The Science desk is a highly collaborative team; editors and reporters work closely together to embrace storytelling forms that resonate with readers, and work in an open and collaborative way with other desks of The Times. The ideal candidate will have a proven ability to translate complex scientific subjects to a general audience, and an appetite for fast, frequent filing at a range of lengths and forms — news, explainers, features, audio and video.

This is an in-office position based in a New York Times bureau in Asia, and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. The location of the role will be discussed with the recruiter during the interview process. Frequent travel will also be required.

Responsibilities:

  • Cover breaking news and produce larger think pieces and cutting-edge features.
  • Write clear, concise, and engaging news stories that adhere to journalistic style guidelines.
  • Use established sources and develop additional ones to land exclusive stories and to cover this beat authoritatively.
  • Monitor news and deliver a steady stream of story ideas that help explain the beat.
  • Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • This role reports to a Science editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years relevant experience in English-language science journalism or communications
  • Proficiency in Mandarin and/or Cantonese
  • Strong sense of journalistic standards, including ethics and news judgment

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Fluent in Mandarin or Cantonese
  • Experience working as a reporter in high-pressure, deadline-driven newsrooms
  • A strong understanding of Times style and standards

  • Responsible for operationally supporting an important set of accounts through the full life-cycle of the business.

  • Lead client contact and coordination with top-tier clients to ensure best-in-class, high-touch service.

And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

The Climate Desk at the New York Times is looking for a high-energy and collaborative journalist to join the team of reporters covering climate and environmental policy and politics.

Climate policy has swung wildly in Washington over the last few years, and we're looking for a reporter who can help readers understand what's happening and why. We want to dig into what's different, who's influencing policymakers and who's benefiting from the shifts and how changing government rules and regulations play out around the country. Our team has a broad mandate for big stories on everything from the National Park Service to the Environmental Protection Agency, from the growth of nuclear power to the Trump administration's war on wind.

You should have a track record of scoops and reporting that has helped to shape the national conversation. You should have a body of work that shows creativity, deep sourcing, broad curiosity, an eye for news and a command of complex ideas.

You should also be a fluid writer who can step back, connect the dots and tell the larger story in compelling ways.

This is an in-office position, based in Washington, D.C. and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Break news on climate and environmental policy, focusing on the E.P.A., the Interior and Energy departments and Congress.

  • Pitch, report and write news and surprising enterprise on climate and environmental policy and politics.

  • Think visually about the most compelling ways to present stories.

  • Contribute to live coverage on breaking news stories.

  • Help readers understand the impact of regulations and the political forces at play.

  • Collaborate with other reporters on news and enterprise.

  • Deliver fast, clean copy in accessible style on complicated topics.

  • Ensure accuracy and clarity.

  • Work collaboratively with members of a multidisciplinary team.

  • Meet tight deadlines and be able to thrive in a daily, unpredictable news environment.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • This role reports to the Deputy Editor, Climate.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience working for a daily news organization

  • 3+ years of demonstrated beat authority

  • A portfolio that demonstrates you are well-versed in current policy, and have a growing circle of expert sources among researchers, policymakers, analysts, public interest groups and lawmakers

  • A portfolio that includes news, enterprise and analysis

  • Crisp, clear, writing skills that also demonstrate a mastery of journalistic style and standards

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Facility with visual and alternative forms of storytelling

  • 8+ years of experience working for a daily news organization
